## Summary

Add regression tests to `tests/sync.test.ts` reproducing both sync-conflict failure modes from WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO (AC1–AC3): (1) same-timestamp divergent copies converge without unbounded `updatedAt` bumping — including `sortIndex`-only conflicts which must never bump (producer Q2); (2) an unattributed soft-delete (`status='deleted'` with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`) never overrides a live remote item; (3) a newer **attributed** delete still propagates. Also adapt the WL-0MT2KZH0I005XUWE deletion-propagation fixtures to attributed deletes (producer Q3 — approved). Drives F2/F3 via red→green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Same-`updatedAt` copies differing only in `sortIndex` merged repeatedly **never bump** `updatedAt` and converge (merged state present on both sides, no unbounded bumping).
- AC2: Same-`updatedAt` copies differing in one non-sortIndex metadata field (e.g. `priority`) converge — `updatedAt` bumps at most once, then stabilises once both sides hold the merged item.
- AC3: Local `status='deleted'` with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` vs remote `status='open'` (both same-timestamp and local-newer different-timestamp) → merged keeps `open`; the merge never produces a soft-deleted item with no attribution.
- AC4: A newer **attributed** delete (non-empty `deletedBy`) still propagates (different-timestamp wins; same-timestamp tie-break still resolves to `deleted`).
- AC5: Existing deletion-propagation tests (WL-0MT2KZH0I005XUWE describe block, tests/sync.test.ts ~L1338) updated to attributed-delete fixtures, preserving their propagation semantics; `npm test` green once F2/F3 land.

## Key Files

- `tests/sync.test.ts`

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `describe('merge convergence & delete protection (WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO)')` to tests/sync.test.ts; reuse the existing `dItem2`-style fixture factory with attribution overrides.
- Convergence assertions loop `mergeWorkItems` calls and assert `updatedAt` is quiescent after the merged state is present on both sides.
- Update WL-0MT2KZH0I005XUWE fixtures to attributed deletes (deletedBy non-empty).

## Summary

Fix the unbounded-`updatedAt` conflict loop: `mergeSameTimestampItems` (src/sync.ts ~L528) currently sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` unconditionally whenever local and remote share a timestamp but diverge in content, so every repeated sync of the same divergent state advances the timestamp with no real user edit behind it. Bump only when the merge actually changed a user-visible field, and **never** bump for `sortIndex`-only conflicts (producer Q2: pure ordering, zero timestamp churn).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Merge changed a user-visible field other than `sortIndex` (mergedFields non-empty beyond sortIndex) → `updatedAt` bumped once; existing lexicographic/local/remote tie-break semantics unchanged.
- AC2: No user-visible field changed (mergedFields empty) → `updatedAt` unchanged.
- AC3: Only `sortIndex` diverged (mergedFields ⊆ {sortIndex}) → `updatedAt` unchanged — sortIndex-only conflicts never bump.
- AC4: Repeated merges of identical divergent state converge with no unbounded bumping (F1 AC1/AC2 regression tests green).

## Key Files

- `src/sync.ts`

## Minimal Implementation

- In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, derive the set of actually-changed user-visible fields from `mergedFields`; bump `updatedAt` only when it contains a field other than `sortIndex`; keep `createdAt` from local. Preserve the existing conflict message/detail reporting.

## Summary

Add delete-side protection mirroring the close-preservation model: treat `status='deleted'` like `status='completed'` — a delete only wins when the deleting side is **attributed** (non-empty `deletedBy` or `deleteReason`) and (for different timestamps) is the **newer** side; otherwise the live non-deleted status is kept. Currently `mergeSameTimestampItems` (~L570) lets any side's `deleted` win unconditionally and `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` (~L805) lets the newer side's `deleted` win purely by recency — so an unattributed soft-delete artifact (empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`, as the field-reported bug) silently overrides a remote `open` item. Covers the delta path too (`replayRemoteDeltaChain` → `mergeWorkItems`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: An unattributed delete on either side never flips a live `open`/`in-progress`/`completed` item to `deleted` (same-timestamp and different-timestamp, both directions).
- AC2: An attributed delete that is the newer change still propagates (F1 AC4 green); a same-timestamp attributed delete still wins deterministically (preserves WL-0MT2KZH0I005XUWE semantics).
- AC3: Both sides deleted (attributed or not) → converges to `deleted` (no live item to protect).
- AC4: F1 AC3/AC4 regression tests green; full `npm test` passes with F1's adapted fixtures (no real-delete regression once F4 attributes real deletes).

## Key Files

- `src/sync.ts`

## Minimal Implementation

- Add an attribution predicate (reuse `isDefaultValue` semantics: `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` non-empty).
- Gate the existing deleted branches in `mergeSameTimestampItems` (~L570) and `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` (~L805): deleted wins only when attributed (+ newer for different-timestamp); unattributed delete falls through to normal resolution so the live status is kept; both-deleted edge converges to `deleted`.

Make intentional deletes **attributed** so they remain propagatable under F3's protection rule (producer Q1 → approved proposed design). `deleteSingle` (packages/shared/src/database.ts ~L1378, exposed via the `node_modules/@worklog/shared` symlink) currently sets `status:'deleted'` + `updatedAt` but never `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`, making every real `wl delete` unattributed — indistinguishable from the merge artifact that caused the field bug. Record `deletedBy` from git identity (reuse the established `getConfiguredUserEmail` pattern) and a `deleteReason`, wiring CLI and REST delete paths, then rebuild the shared package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `Database.delete(id, recursive?, opts?: { deletedBy?: string; deleteReason?: string })` accepts optional attribution (backwards compatible); `deleteSingle` persists non-empty attribution.
- AC2: CLI `wl delete` (src/commands/delete.ts) records `deletedBy` from git identity plus a default `deleteReason`; REST DELETE (src/api.ts) passes request identity; recursive deletion attributes descendants too.

# Intake Brief: Remove OpenBrain (WL-0MTH28WDS008WMXA)

## Problem statement

OpenBrain is an optional integration (`src/openbrain.ts`) that spawns the `ob` CLI to submit a summary whenever a work item is marked completed. This project enabled it for local testing (`openBrainEnabled: true` in `.worklog/config.yaml`, commit `66fb51a8`) but the `ob` binary is not installed, so every `wl update`/`wl close` that completes an item emits `[openbrain] ...` errors to stderr. The integration is unused and, per producer confirmation, is to be **removed entirely** — both from the shared codebase and from this project's config.

## Users

- **Developers** running `wl update`/`wl close` in this project — they see stray `[openbrain]` errors and want clean output.
- **Worklog maintainers** — they want dead integration code (which requires an `ob` binary nobody has and whose `wl openbrain` commands were never implemented) removed from the shared CLI.

User stories:
- As a developer in this project, I want `wl update` to complete a work item without emitting `[openbrain]` errors, so my terminal output is clean.
- As a Worklog maintainer, I want the OpenBrain integration absent from the shared codebase, so there is no dead code and no misleading docs/plugin references.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Feature removed from the shared codebase**: `src/openbrain.ts` deleted; `submitToOpenBrain` imports and call sites removed from `src/commands/update.ts` and `src/commands/close.ts`; `openBrainEnabled` removed from `WorklogConfig` in `packages/shared/src/types.ts`.
2. **Project-scoped disablement**: `openBrainEnabled: true` removed from `.worklog/config.yaml` in this repository.
3. **No dangling references or dead artifacts**: `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts`, `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts`, and `docs/openbrain.md` deleted; OpenBrain references removed from `CLI.md` and `README.md`. A repo-wide search (`rg -i "openbrain|submitToOpenBrain|openBrainEnabled"`) returns no matches in tracked source/docs (excluding git history and regenerated `dist/` artifacts).
4. **Error gone**: completing a work item via `wl update` and `wl close` in this project produces no `[openbrain]` stderr output (validated by the CLI test run, AC5).
5. **Green build & docs**: full project test suite passes with the new changes; all related documentation reflects the removal (README, CLI.md, code comments, docs table).

## Constraints

- No behavior changes beyond removing the OpenBrain path — `wl close`/`wl update` semantics (recursive close, re-sort, audit handling) are untouched.
- Worktrees under `.worklog/worktrees/*` are separate feature branches — do not edit them in this change; only the main checkout is in scope.
- Config user file `.worklog/config.yaml` is the only place `openBrainEnabled` is set in this repo; `config.defaults.yaml` does not set it (verify at implementation time).
- The optional retry-queue file `.worklog/openbrain-queue.jsonl` may exist from failed submissions; it is transient data, not code — no action required beyond optionally removing it.

## Existing state

- `src/openbrain.ts` implements `submitToOpenBrain()` (spawns `ob add --stdin --title …`), `buildOpenBrainSummary()`, `appendToQueue()` (retry queue), and `resolveObBinary()` (`WL_OB_BIN` or `ob`).
- `src/commands/update.ts`: calls `submitToOpenBrain(item)` when `updates.status === 'completed'` and `config.openBrainEnabled`.
- `src/commands/close.ts`: calls `submitToOpenBrain(updated)` from the force, audit-gated recursive, and standard close paths when `config.openBrainEnabled`; the recovery path comments reference OpenBrain.
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts`: `WorklogConfig` declares `openBrainEnabled?: boolean`.
- `.worklog/config.yaml`: `openBrainEnabled: true`.
- Docs: `docs/openbrain.md`; `CLI.md` lists `wl openbrain status/resubmit` (commands were never implemented); `README.md` docs table links `docs/openbrain.md`.
- Tests: `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts`, `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts`.
- `ob` is not on PATH and `WL_OB_BIN` is unset; the globally installed `wl` (`/usr/local/bin/wl`) symlinks to this repo's built `dist/cli.js`, so a rebuild is required to actually stop the errors.

## Desired change

Remove the OpenBrain integration and its project config toggle:

- Delete `src/openbrain.ts`, `docs/openbrain.md`, `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts`, `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts`.
- In `src/commands/update.ts` / `src/commands/close.ts`: drop the `submitToOpenBrain` import and every `openBrainEnabled` fire-and-forget block (including the recovery-path comment).
- In `packages/shared/src/types.ts`: remove `openBrainEnabled?: boolean`.
- In `.worklog/config.yaml`: remove `openBrainEnabled: true`.
- In `CLI.md` / `README.md`: remove OpenBrain references.
- Rebuild (`npm run build:shared && npm run build`) so the installed `wl` no longer ships `openbrain.js` in `dist/`.

## Key Files:

- `src/openbrain.ts` — delete (entire module)
- `src/commands/update.ts` — remove import + completion call block
- `src/commands/close.ts` — remove import + three close-path call blocks + recovery comment
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` — remove `openBrainEnabled` from `WorklogConfig`
- `.worklog/config.yaml` — remove `openBrainEnabled: true`
- `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts` — delete
- `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts` — delete
- `docs/openbrain.md` — delete
- `docs/feature-requests/openbrain-playwright-fallback-retrieval.md` — delete (OpenBrain feature request; would fail AC3 repo-wide search)
- `CLI.md`, `README.md` — remove OpenBrain references

## Related work

- WL-0MNM4SDMA000GOBC — "Whenever a work item is marked as completed/done update OpenBrain": introduced the integration (predecessor).
- WL-0MOHP1FIP007LYCB — "Make wl close OpenBrain submission fully non-blocking": changed the close flow (predecessor).
- WL-0MNRPS89H004COB0 — "Fix validator and openbrain test failures": fixed CLI.md docs + EPIPE handling (predecessor).

# Dispatch-logs Skill: Generate Global Dispatch Reports

A `/skill:dispatch-logs` command that produces a concise, human-readable (or JSON) 24-hour dispatch activity report across all projects on the machine — including leader state, timeline, errors, and coordination status — with support for custom time windows and per-project filtering.

## Problem Statement

Operators investigating overnight dispatches must manually aggregate `*/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` files across all projects on the machine. There is no single command to produce a concise 24-hour (or custom window) global dispatch report.

## Users

- **Operator on-call**: Needs a quick view of what dispatches ran overnight and whether any errors occurred.
- **Debugging engineer**: Tracing a specific dispatch failure across projects.
- **Team lead**: Reviewing dispatch activity trends over a custom time window.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `/skill:dispatch-logs` produces a human-readable report covering all projects on the machine for the last 24 hours (default window).
2. All invocation flags work correctly: `--hours N`, `--since`/`--until` ISO timestamps, `--project <name>`, and `--json` for machine-readable output.
3. The report includes five sections: (a) leader summary, (b) dispatch timeline, (c) error summary, (d) coordination state, and (e) known issues.
4. Gracefully handles the case when no dispatch logs exist (produces an empty/clean report, not an error).
5. Unit tests pass for log parsing, argument handling, and report structure (using mocked log files).
6. SKILL.md is complete with name, description, invocation examples, and frontmatter.

## Constraints

- Log files are in JSONL format (one JSON object per line).
- Machine coordination state lives in `~/.herdr/downtime/` (two JSON files).
- Must skip `node_modules`, `dist`, `build` directories during project root discovery.
- Default window is 24 hours from `Date.now()`; custom windows use ISO 8601 timestamps.

## Existing State

- Per-worklog dispatch logs exist at `*/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.
- Machine-wide coordination at `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` and `downtime-leader-lease.json`.
- Companion debug item (WL-0MTJPYM53003ORCV) adds per-strike stderr/exitCode — the dispatch-logs skill should note when this data is unavailable.

## Desired Change

Create a new skill in `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/` with:
- `SKILL.md` — skill definition with frontmatter and invocation docs.
- `scripts/dispatch-logs.py` — Python script implementing the report generation.
- `tests/dispatch-logs.test.py` — unit tests with mocked data.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/SKILL.md` — New skill definition file.
- `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/scripts/dispatch-logs.py` — Core logic: argument parsing, log discovery, parsing, report generation.
- `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/tests/dispatch-logs.test.py` — Unit tests.
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` — Read-only coordination state.
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-leader-lease.json` — Read-only leader lease.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep**: Resist adding extra report sections beyond the five specified (leader summary, dispatch timeline, error summary, coordination state, known issues).
- **Discovery performance**: Walking from `~` to find all project roots could be slow on machines with many repositories; consider caching or a configurable root list.
- **JSONL format consistency**: Assumes all projects write logs in the same JSONL format; malformed lines should be skipped gracefully.
- **Coordination files**: Assumes `~/.herdr/downtime/` files are present and readable; handle missing files gracefully.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MTJPYM53003ORCV** — "Downtime dispatcher: make wl-error pauses debuggable" (companion; provides richer per-strike data the dispatch-logs skill should report on).
- **WL-0MU4URK4H006OFCE** — "Extend dispatch log schema and add pane lifecycle monitor" (may affect log parsing).
- **WL-0MU8808ZY0091JIA** — "Downtime dispatcher: log the actual no-dispatch reason" (enriches available log data).
- **WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8** — "Log herdr downtime dispatches" (established the per-worklog log architecture).

# Investigate downtime dispatcher vs herdr selection list divergence (WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q)

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher consistently selects and dispatches work items that do not appear in the herdr extensions selection list, so two first-class "next most important item" selectors disagree. The project needs a diagnosed root cause for the divergence and a producer-reviewed determination of which ranking (if either) correctly identifies the most important item, before any fix is scoped.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — needs a single trustworthy "most important" ordering to decide what to work on and whether downtime dispatch is helping or harming prioritization.
- **Agent / herdr user** browsing `prefix+l` — relies on the herdr list as the visible priority queue; unexpected downtime work on off-list items erodes trust in the list.
- **Maintainer of wl next / herdr / downtime-worker** — needs a clear contract for how the two selectors should relate (shared vs intentionally different).

Example user stories:
- "As a producer, I want the downtime dispatcher and the herdr list to agree on priority, so automated work tracks my intent."
- "As a herdr user, when downtime dispatches `/skill:implement WL-XYZ`, I want WL-XYZ to have been visible in the herdr list, so I understand why it was chosen."
- "As a maintainer, I want a documented ranking contract so I can tell whether a divergence is a bug or an intentional tier policy."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Divergence diagnosed with evidence** — the brief/records cite the exact code paths compared (herdr `fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` + `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` + `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` vs downtime `downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork` + `src/commands/next.ts` + `packages/shared/src/database.ts:filterCandidates/findNextWorkItemFromItems/computeScore/reSort`) and a reproducible sample where the two selectors disagree (e.g. `wl next -n N` output vs herdr rendered list vs downtime tier chosen).
2. **Ranking gap mapped** — each material difference is listed: input sets/caps (`wl next -n` cap 32 + mandatory merge vs stage-scoped `wl next --stage …` per tier + `wl list` for audit), stage/risk/effort filters, audit-tier recency/marker/code-freeze gates, blocked/in_review handling, `sortIndex`/reSort/recency-policy, and grouping vs flat ordering.
3. **"Most important" determination recorded and producer-reviewed** — the work item records which selector (herdr list, dispatcher tier order, or `wl next` score) is judged authoritative for "most important" and why, with an explicit producer sign-off comment; if neither is authoritative, the desired unified ranking is described.
4. **Follow-up work item(s) filed only after review** — no fix is implemented in this investigation; at most, one or more follow-up work items are created *after* producer review to align or intentionally diverge the selectors, with the resolution direction noted on this item.
5. **Documentation/tests note** — the investigation updates or points to the doc that will carry the ranking contract (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` / herdr README / `src/commands/next.ts` help), and any sampling scripts are reproducible.

## Constraints

- Investigation only — do not change ranking code in this item; any code change requires a separate work item after producer review.
- Do not assume which selector is correct; ask the producer when the evidence is ambiguous.
- Respect ignore rules; keep questions high-signal (≤3 per round).
- All description/comments in Markdown; escape only backticks.

## Existing state

- **Herdr list:** `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` runs `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` (auto `reSort` unless `--no-re-sort`), merges mandatory subsets from `wl list --priority critical --root-only` and `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` via `fetchMandatorySubsets`, applies `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` (root-only, `stage != done`, mandatory always shown, `browseItemCount` limits only "other" items), and regroups with `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` / `assignItemGroups` (critical Group N / Group N / Idea / Other / In Review, file-path conflict partitioning). Rendering via `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.

- **wl next ranking (shared):** `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `reSort()` = `getAllOrderedByScore(recencyPolicy)` → `assignSortIndexValues`; `computeScore` weights priority×1000, `blocksHighPriority` +500, `in_review` +600, age/effort/recency, blocked −10000, in-progress multipliers; audit-not-ready fresh boost +3500 (non-critical only); `filterCandidates` pipeline (stage → deleted → completed/done/in_review preservation → in_progress → excluded → assignee/search → risk/effort at-most → dep-blocked); `handleCriticalEscalation` (unblocked criticals first, then blocked-critical blockers), non-critical blocker surfacing, open-item `selectBySortIndex` (sortIndex or effective-priority tie-break). `src/commands/next.ts` auto reSort with `--recency-policy` (default `ignore`) and risk/effort filters.

- **Downtime dispatcher:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork` — tier order: audit (`wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` within 7-day recency, no valid audit within 7d, root-only, durable dispatched-marker exclusion, active-audit single-flight), implement (`wl next --stage plan_complete --risk ≤Medium --effort ≤Medium`, open + blocked filtering), plan (`wl next --stage intake_complete`), fallback idea (`wl next --stage idea`); pre-dispatch CAS claim (`--if-status/--if-stage`), per-process single-flight, code-freeze tri-state gate (frozen/ambiguous skips audit+implement, reports `code-freeze`/`fresh-audit-skip`/`audit-in-flight`/`wl-error`/`no-candidate`), scheduled-prompts tier, round-robin tie-break, 60-min no-candidate cooldown, 3-strike `wl-error` pause, per-worklog rolling log + machine-wide coordination lease.

- Observed sample (2026-09-02): `wl next -n 20` returned Idea-group high-priority items (e.g. WL-0MT... high/idea) while herdr's mandatory set adds 19 `in_review` + critical groups; dispatcher tiers can select items outside the herdr window due to stage/risk scoping and audit-tier `wl list` source.

## Desired change

For this investigation: a producer-reviewed brief on this work item that (a) explains why the two selectors diverge, (b) judges which (if either) currently picks the most important item, and (c) scopes the follow-up direction (unify on `wl next` score vs keep intentional tier divergence vs new contract). No code change in this item.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — herdr list fetch: `wl next -n` + mandatory `wl list` merge + `selectWorkItems`/`regroupWorkItems`
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — mandatory-always logic (critical ∪ completed/in_review, root-only, done excluded)
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — `assignItemGroups`/`regroupWorkItems` ordering (Critical Group N / Group N / Idea / Other / In Review)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — list rendering consuming grouped selection
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier orchestration, claim/marker/freeze gates
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `computeScore`/`filterCandidates`/`findNextWorkItemFromItems`/`handleCriticalEscalation`/`reSort`/`selectBySortIndex`
- `src/commands/next.ts` / `src/commands/grouping.ts` — `wl next` entry point, auto reSort, stage/risk/effort filters, group assignment
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` / `packages/herdr/README.md` / `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — ranking/coordination contract docs

## Related work

- **WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX** — counts in Herdr selection list are incorrect (open, high) — reporting that the list's top-N vs group totals disagree ( symptom of mandatory-merge/wl-next-cap interaction)
- **WL-0MS8XL3EW006Y04G** — Herdr selection list: smart selection (completed) — introduced mandatory-always + fetch merge
- **WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW / WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G / WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR** — in_review/completed visibility and root-only rules shaping mandatory set
- **WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 / WL-0MSMAIP5F003WAGG** — implement tier + risk/effort filters as wired into `wl next` and downtime dispatch
- **WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY / WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN / WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8** — dispatched-marker exclusion, conditional claim, dispatch logging
- **WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6** — priority-first with round-robin tie-break (shared round-robin cursor)
- **WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2** — spare-capacity dispatch (N slots vs all-slots-free)
- **WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94 / WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW** — collapsible group headings / regroup to avoid duplicate headings
- RCA: `downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md`, `downtime-disable-incident-rca-2026-08-22.md` — tier order, re-dispatch loop, code-freeze gate

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "selection list" means herdr `prefix+l` Work Items list (`fetchNextItems` path); "downtime dispatcher" means `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier loop in `downtime-worker.ts`.
- Assumption: producer wants a single notion of "most important" but may accept intentional divergence (e.g. audit tier outranking open high-priority work) — to be confirmed in review.
- Risk: `sortIndex` staleness and `--recency-policy` differences can make samples non-reproducible; mitigate by recording the exact `wl` commands and whether `reSort` ran.
- Risk: per-worklog vs machine-wide coordination state split can confuse which item was "most important globally" vs per-worklog — note the scope in the determination.
- Scope-creep risk: unifying ranking touches `wl next` scoring, herdr selection, and downtime tiers — keep this item to investigation only; file separate implementation items after review.

## Producer determination — revised 2026-09-02 (WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1)

**Revised: Herdr extension selection list is canonical; dispatcher selects the list head.** Supersedes WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS (`wl next` / `computeScore`/`reSort` as canonical). Follow-up rescoped to **WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2**: downtime dispatcher should not calculate its own ordering — it should simply select the first item in the Herdr selection list (`fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` → `worklist.ts`). All selection criteria already live in that list; consuming the head makes the two selectors agree by construction. Any remaining safety gates (code-freeze, dispatched-marker, single-flight) act as filters on the Herdr-ordered candidates, not as a competing ranking. Q1 most-important = Herdr list order; Q2 unify by Herdr list as single source of truth.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When you say 'most important,' do you mean the `wl next` score order (priority/age/blocking/audit boost) or the downtime tier order (audit → implement → plan → idea)?" — **Revised 2026-09-02 (WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): Herdr extension selection list order is authoritative** (`fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems`). Supersedes 2026-09-02 WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS. Dispatcher should select the first item in the Herdr list — no second ranking.
- Q2: "Should the two selectors be unified to one shared ranking, or should the dispatcher intentionally differ (e.g. audit-first) and the herdr list stay as-is?" — **Revised 2026-09-02 (WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): unified on the Herdr list** — single source of truth; dispatcher consumes the list head. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`".
- Q3: "For sampling, which `browseItemCount` / `wl next -n` window and which worklog root should be the reference?" — **Answer (resolved 2026-09-02, Producer): LGTM** — default `browseItemCount`/ContextHub root/`wl next -n 20` accepted.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSB3NYMW008APQC** – Tests: pane visibility detection module (visibility.test.ts) (completed)
- **WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ** – Herdr selection list: no indication of items below the fold (completed)

# Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2)

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork`) and the Herdr extension selection list (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` → `worklist.ts`) disagree on "most important item" because the dispatcher maintains its own tier ordering (`wl next --stage …` per tier + `wl list` audit query) instead of reusing the Herdr list. The project needs the dispatcher to consume the Herdr list head so the two selectors agree by construction. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`" scope per producer determination WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 (2026-09-02).

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — needs a single trustworthy queue; the item dispatched during downtime was visible at the top of `prefix+l` and reflects declared prioritization intent.
- **Herdr user browsing `prefix+l`** — expects downtime work to track exactly what the visible list shows, so automated work does not appear arbitrary.
- **Maintainer of herdr / downtime-worker / wl next** — needs a single ranking contract; ranking logic lives only in the fetcher/smart-selection/grouping/database pipeline.

Example user stories:
- As a producer, I want the downtime dispatcher to pick the first item shown in the Herdr list, so automated work follows the priority I already see.
- As a herdr user, when downtime dispatches `/skill:implement WL-XYZ`, I want WL-XYZ to have been at the head of the Herdr list, so I understand why it was chosen.
- As a maintainer, I want the ranking contract documented as "dispatcher == Herdr list head" so future safety gates are evaluated as filters, not a competing ranking.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dispatcher consumes Herdr list head** — `dispatchDowntimeWork` (and any coordination-leader path) derives its candidate from the Herdr selection list head rather than a separate tier ordering / stage-scoped `wl next` / `wl list` audit query. No second ranking implementation remains on the dispatch path.
2. **No duplicate ranking; gates are filters** — tier ordering / `wl next --stage` per-tier calls / audit `wl list` ranking are no longer used to pick "most important". Any safety gates that must remain (code-freeze skip, dispatched-marker exclusion, active-audit single-flight, per-process single-flight / CAS claim) act as sequential filters on the Herdr-ordered candidates. If no Herdr-ordered candidate passes the filters, the dispatcher reports "no candidate" rather than falling back to a separate ranking.
3. **Herdr list remains sole ranking path** — `fetchNextItems` / `selectWorkItems` / `regroupWorkItems` stay the sole ranking path (mandatory-always for critical + `completed`/`in_review`, `browseItemCount` windowing of "other" items, grouping logic, `reSort`/`computeScore` as used by the fetcher). No `wl next`/`database.ts` scoring change is required to fix the divergence; if `fetchNextItems` delegates to `wl next` internally that internal detail is acceptable — the observable contract is "dispatcher == Herdr list head".
4. **Contract documented** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` (and `src/commands/next.ts` help if it references dispatcher selection) state explicitly: dispatcher selects the first dispatchable item from the Herdr selection list; any remaining safety override (e.g. code-freeze) is documented as a skip/filter on that sequence, not a ranking.
5. **No regression; observable agreement proven** — existing `wl next` / herdr fetcher/grouping / downtime-worker fixtures pass; a reproducible sampling script shows `wl next -n` / Herdr list / downtime pick agree (downtime picks the list head after filtering) on a fixture. Dispatched-marker / code-freeze / single-flight gating still respected as filters on the Herdr sequence.

## Constraints

- Zero npm deps for herdr; `smart-selection.ts`/`grouping.ts` duplicated per TUI stays in sync with `src/commands/*` if touched.
- `browseItemCount` clamping (1–50) and root-only / `done`-exclusion rules respected.
- Do not fork a second ranking; reuse the Herdr list pipeline.
- Investigation only touched the prior item (WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q); this item carries the implementation.
- Backwards compat: existing dispatched-marker / code-freeze gating semantics preserved as filters.

## Existing state

- **Herdr list:** `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` runs `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` (auto `reSort` unless `--no-re-sort`), merges mandatory subsets via `fetchMandatorySubsets` (`wl list --priority critical --root-only` and `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`), applies `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` (root-only, `stage != done`, mandatory always shown, `browseItemCount` limits only "other" items), and regroups with `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` / `assignItemGroups` (Critical Group N / Group N / Idea / Other / In Review). Rendered via `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- **Downtime dispatcher:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork` — tier order audit → implement (`wl next --stage plan_complete` with risk/effort caps) → plan (`wl next --stage intake_complete`) → fallback idea (`wl next --stage idea`); audit tier uses `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` with 7-day recency / dispatched-marker / active-audit / code-freeze gates; pre-dispatch CAS claim, per-process single-flight, scheduled-prompts tier, round-robin cursor, cooldowns.
- **Shared scoring:** `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (`computeScore`/`reSort`/`filterCandidates`/`findNextWorkItemFromItems`) and `src/commands/next.ts` auto `reSort` — shared by `wl next` but not required to change for this contract; the observable contract is Herdr list head.
- All divergence gaps mapped in WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q (cap 32 / mandatory merge / stage-scoped calls / audit `wl list` source / tier order / risk-effort gates / code-freeze tri-state, etc.) — eliminated by consuming the Herdr order directly.

## Desired change

Replace the dispatcher's independent tier ordering with consumption of the Herdr selection list head:

- Refactor `downtime-worker.ts` to invoke (or share code with) the Herdr fetcher/selection pipeline to obtain the ordered candidate sequence, then apply only the necessary safety filters (code-freeze, dispatched-marker, single-flight/active-audit) sequentially on that sequence.
- Remove or dead-code the tier-ordering / per-stage `wl next` / audit `wl list` ranking path from the dispatch decision (or leave only as unused fallback behind a feature flag with a clear deprecation note).
- Document the contract ("dispatcher == Herdr list head; filters, not ranking") in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — Herdr selection pipeline reused by dispatcher
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — mandatory-always + browseItemCount logic
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — regroupWorkItems / assignItemGroups ordering
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — rendering consuming grouped selection
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatchDowntimeWork to be refactored to consume list head (+ fixtures)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — computeScore/reSort/filterCandidates as used by fetcher (not dispatcher ranking)
- `src/commands/next.ts` / `src/commands/grouping.ts` — wl next entry point as used by fetcher
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatcher contract doc
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr list contract doc

## Related work

- Investigation: WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q — downtime dispatcher vs herdr selection list divergence (producer determination revised 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1, superseding WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS) → follow-up direction is this item.
- WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX — counts in Herdr selection list are incorrect (symptom of cap/mandatory interaction; not blocking but shares fetcher context)
- WL-0MS8XL3EW006Y04G / WL-0MSKCRX730052iiw / WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G / WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR — Herdr smart selection / in_review / root-only rules shaping mandatory set
- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 / WL-0MSMAIP5F003WAGG — implement tier + risk/effort filters wired into wl next / dispatcher (removed or converted to filters in this work)
- WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY / WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN / WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 — dispatched-marker exclusion, conditional claim, dispatch logging (preserved as filters)
- WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6 — priority-first with round-robin tie-break (cursor handling to reconcile with Herdr order)
- RCA docs: `downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md`, `downtime-disable-incident-rca-2026-08-22.md` — prior tier/re-dispatch incidents

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "selection list" means herdr `prefix+l` Work Items list (`fetchNextItems` path); "downtime dispatcher" means `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier loop in `downtime-worker.ts` (including coordination leader path if any).
- Assumption: producer wants a single notion of "most important" — confirmed 2026-09-02 (Herdr list canonical; dispatcher consumes head).
- Risk: code-freeze / audit safety behavior at head — if the list head must be skipped, the skip order must be explicit and remain a filter on the Herdr sequence; document clearly.
- Risk: `in_review` mandatory-always items in the list — dispatcher taking the head must still respect `completed`/`in_review` dispatchability; filter vs ranking distinction must be explicit to avoid re-dispatching audits.
- Risk: spare-capacity / idle-budget / round-robin cursor logic must be reconciled as filters or removed; otherwise a second ordering re-emerges.
- Scope-creep risk: unifying ranking touches herdr selection and downtime-worker — keep scope to dispatcher-consumes-head; do not rework scoring or grouping unless required for the contract. Extra opportunities → new work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When you say 'most important,' do you mean the Herdr list order or the dispatcher tier order?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1, rescoping WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2; supersedes WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS): **Herdr extension selection list order is authoritative** (`fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems`). Dispatcher selects the first item in that list — no second ranking. Source: producer comment WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 on WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q.
- Q2: "Should the two selectors be unified to one shared ranking, or should the dispatcher intentionally differ (e.g. audit-first)?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): **Unified on the Herdr list** — single source of truth; dispatcher consumes the list head. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`". Source: same producer determination.
- Q3: "For sampling, which `browseItemCount` / `wl next -n` window and which worklog root should be the reference?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS as affirmed by WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): **LGTM** — default `browseItemCount` / ContextHub root / `wl next -n 20` accepted as sampling reference. Source: producer comment on WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q.

No open questions. Interview skipped — seed context and revised producer determination (WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1) already provide a clear, testable brief.

# Scheduled prompts: add time-of-day dispatch (time window) to scheduled-prompts tier

## Problem statement

The scheduled-prompts tier (WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX; `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, `templates/scheduled-prompts.json`) only supports best-effort frequency in whole days (`intervalDays` via `isDueScheduledPrompt`: due iff `now - lastTriggeredAt >= intervalDays`). There is no way to pin a prompt to a time of day, so a daily standup cannot be made to run at a specific wall-clock time (e.g. 06:05) and instead fires whenever the next idle slot appears after the interval elapses — too early/late for a daily standup window.

## Users

- Operators who want a prompt (notably the daily standup, `/skill:standup`) to run at a specific time of day, not just once per N days whenever an idle slot appears.

### User stories

- As an operator, I want to add an optional `time` field (e.g. `06:05`) to a scheduled-prompt entry so the system dispatches it in the first available idle window **after** that time, so the standup runs at 06:05 each day.
- As an operator, when `time` is absent the existing behaviour is unchanged (due iff `now - last >= intervalDays`), so existing entries like `/skill:refactor` keep working without config changes.
- As an operator, I want `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` and provisioned `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` to set `/skill:standup` to 06:05, so a fresh worklog gets the correct daily standup time.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add optional `time?: string` to `ScheduledPrompt` (`packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts`). When absent, behaviour is identical to today (backward-compatible). Valid values are wall-clock `HH:MM` 24-hour times (e.g. `06:05`); entries with an invalid `time` are skipped with a logged warning (fail-closed, never a crash), consistent with invalid `intervalDays`/prompt handling (AC7 of WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX).
2. Extend due-check semantics (`isDueScheduledPrompt` / `getDueScheduledPrompt`): an entry with `time` is due only when BOTH (a) `now - lastTriggeredAt >= intervalDays * DAY_MS` (same interval gate as today) AND (b) `now` is at or after the `time` on the calendar day of `now` (local wall-clock). If `now` is before `time` today and the interval gate is otherwise satisfied, the entry is NOT due — it becomes due in the first idle window at/after `time`. A dispatched entry is NOT due again until the next calendar day's `time` has been reached and the interval has again elapsed (so a 06:05 daily entry dispatched at 07:00 today is not due again at 08:00 today).
3. `lastTriggeredAt` semantics ensure once-per-interval: after a timed dispatch, the interval comparison uses the actual dispatch time, so a missed `time` (e.g. no idle slot until 08:00) still counts as dispatched for that day and the next due time is tomorrow 06:05 (not 08:00 tomorrow and not immediately). Daily entries with `time` therefore fire at most once per calendar day.
4. Update `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` to include `/skill:standup` with `intervalDays: 1` and `time: "06:05"` (the canonical standup time). `src/commands/init.ts` provisioning remains create-if-absent; `wl init` on an existing repo must not clobber user edits — if the operator has customised scheduled prompts, re-running `wl init` leaves them untouched. New worklogs provisioned after this change get the timed standup entry.
5. Ensure `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` in the current checkout reflects `time: "06:05"` for `/skill:standup` (so the dev branch's live config matches the template).
6. Update documentation/comments to describe the `time` field (README / `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` header / `PLUGIN_GUIDE.md` or equivalent downtime docs) and the "first window after time" semantics, including the backward-compat note when `time` is absent and the local wall-clock interpretation of `HH:MM`.
7. Unit/integration tests cover: parse of `time` (valid, absent, invalid → skipped), due-check with `time` (before-time not due, at/after-time due, interval gate interaction, once-per-day, missed-window becomes tomorrow), backward-compat (no `time` behaves as before), and the timed standup entry in the provisioned template.
8. Full project test suite passes with the new changes (no regressions).

## Constraints

- Follow the worker's existing fail-closed philosophy at every boundary: never dispatch, never throw (mirrors WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX constraints and `scheduled-prompts.ts` header).
- `time` is wall-clock local `HH:MM` (no timezone field, no cron); `lastTriggeredAt` remains UTC ISO-8601 as today. The due check interprets `time` against local calendar day.
- Scheduled tier remains the first dispatch tier, gated by the same fresh-read code-freeze marker; per-process single-flight guard still applies. No new timer infrastructure — reuse `createDowntimeWorker.tick`.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — `ScheduledPrompt` (id/prompt/intervalDays/lastTriggeredAt), `parseScheduledPrompt`, `isDueScheduledPrompt`, `getDueScheduledPrompt`, `DAY_MS`; no `time` field.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` scheduled tier (freeze gate → scheduled → audit → …); `dispatchScheduledPrompt` with atomic `lastTriggeredAt` persist + rolling-log `scheduled` kind.
- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` + `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — base set is `/skill:refactor` (intervalDays 3) plus `/skill:standup` (intervalDays 1) with no `time`.
- `src/commands/init.ts` — provisions `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` from the template, create-if-absent (never clobber).

## Desired change

Extend `ScheduledPrompt` with optional `time: "HH:MM"` and update the due-check to be "interval gate AND at-or-after time today" so timed entries dispatch in the first idle window after their wall-clock time. Set the canonical standup time to `06:05` in both the template and the live `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`. Update docs/tests accordingly. When `time` is absent, behaviour is identical to today.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — add `time` field, validation, due-check extension.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — no structural change expected (consumes via `getDueScheduledPrompt`), but verify tier interaction / dispatch semantics for timed entries.
- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` — add `time: "06:05"` to `/skill:standup`.
- `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — add `time: "06:05"` to `/skill:standup` in the checkout so the dev branch reflects the template.
- `src/commands/init.ts` — no change expected beyond carrying the new template value (create-if-absent preserved).
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.test.ts` or `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` / `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — new/updated tests for `time` parse + due-check.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` / `PLUGIN_GUIDE.md` / `CONFIG.md` / `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` header — document `time` field and "first window after time" semantics.

## Related work

- WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX — scheduled prompts tier (parent capability).
- Standup skill: `/skill:standup` + `generate_standup.py` (scheduled via this tier; canonical consumer of `06:05`).
- WL-0MTF5UAJ4000LLZ9 — provisioning / scheduled-prompts template.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: `time` is `HH:MM` local wall-clock on the calendar day of `now`; seconds are not needed. `lastTriggeredAt` remains UTC — the due check bridges them by comparing the local clock for `time` against `now` and the interval against `lastTriggeredAt`.
- Risk: "first window after time" depends on an idle slot appearing; if the machine is busy all day, the dispatch slips to the next idle window (still at most once per day due to `lastTriggeredAt` anchoring). This is the correct best-effort behaviour.
- Risk: DST / system clock skew — acceptable for best-effort `HH:MM` local semantics; clock-skew handling mirrors `isDueScheduledPrompt` today (future `lastTriggeredAt` → not due).
- Scope creep: cron expressions, timezone-aware schedules, per-entry model overrides — record separately, not this item.

## Problem statement

Downtime coordination entries expire via `pruneStaleEntries(coordinationDir, leaseTtlMs)` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchFromCoordination` (`leaseTtlMs = DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS*1000 = 300s`). But `runCoordinationCheckIn` re-offers only every `DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS = 30min`. A non-leader's entry is offered at most once per 30min yet is pruned after 5min if no dispatch consumes it — 25min dead window where the leader sees no entry for that project.

Overnight this starved SorraAgents while ContextHub dispatched alone every ~30min (verified Sep 4: SorraAgents offered `SA-0MSQ6K7Z1002H14Z` at 06:39:39 -> dispatched 06:39:41 only when offer was fresh; earlier offers at 23:45,00:08,00:38 etc. were pruned before the next idle dispatch). The `critical first then round-robin (per-worklogRoot)` guarantee (`WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V` + =`WL-0MTJE0FXC006WAOX`) never got a chance — `sortEntriesByRoundRobin` only orders entries that are present.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — expects global `critical first, then round-robin across projects` as documented; overnight bias to one project erodes trust and delays other projects' ready work.
- **Herdr user with multiple project tabs open** — wants spare-capacity dispatch shared fairly, not oversubscribing one project's backlog.
- **Maintainer of herdr / downtime-worker / wl** — needs a single consistent contract for cross-project dispatch without TTL/check-in mismatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Expiry removed** — `pruneStaleEntries` (and any equivalent TTL prune on `downtime-coordination.json`) is removed or disabled for the machine coordination file. No coordination entry is removed solely by wall-clock age. Legacy per-worklog files (if still read) follow the same rule.
2. **Dispatch checks current eligibility** — before dispatching, the dispatcher re-fetches the work item via `fetchItem(workItemId, worklogRoot)` and verifies it is still in a dispatchable state (`classifyItemForDispatch` / `isAuditFresh` / stage+status that needs work). A stale entry (item now closed/in_progress/done, audit now fresh, or otherwise not dispatchable) is treated as non-dispatchable: its entry is removed, the cursor is not advanced for it, and the dispatcher continues to the next entry — no pane spawned, no marker written.
   - Existing safety gates preserved as filters: code-freeze skip, dispatched-marker exclusion, single-flight/CAS claim, per-process single-flight remain and act as filters on the coordination-ordered candidates.
   - If no entry passes the fresh eligibility check, dispatcher reports `no-candidate` (probe semantics unchanged by `WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7` — coordination file emptiness is a transient offer gap, not a backlog signal).
3. **Global ordering preserved** — tier order `audit -> critical (sortIndex) -> implement -> plan -> intake` across worklogRoots, with `sortEntriesByRoundRobin` / `downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` for same-tier non-critical entries (unknown roots first, oldest timestamp first). One dispatch per idle window still advances `advanceRoundRobinCursor` only for the dispatched root.
4. **Not blocked on independent work** — do not touch scoring/rank reuse (`WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2` owns `dispatcher == Herdr list head`); if that lands first, merge cleanly without reintroducing a second ranking.
5. **Tests & build green** — existing `downtime-worker` / coordination / round-robin fixtures updated (prune tests removed or inverted, eligibility re-check tests added); `npm run build` + herdr suite green. Manual spot: overnight log shows SorraAgents offer is not lost before dispatch.
6. **Docs updated** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` downtime section describe the new contract: entries do not expire, dispatch validates eligibility at dispatch time.

## Constraints

- Do not introduce a second ranking; reuse existing `fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` / `computeMostImportantItem` pipeline for eligibility where possible — ranking contract is Herdr list head (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2).
- Fail-safe: unreadable coordination/lease files still degrade to no dispatch this cycle, never crash.
- No deps change; herdr stays zero npm deps for fetcher path if touched.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts:pruneStaleEntries` + `downtime-worker.ts:dispatchFromCoordination` prune at every dispatch cycle (`leaseTtlMs=300s` from `leader-election.ts:DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS`).
- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` 5-min lease (`downtime-leader-lease.json`) — leadership only, not coordination entry TTL.
- `downtime-worker.ts:runCoordinationCheckIn` check-in 30min (`DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS`), `DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS` / `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_STALE_WINDOW_MS` etc. as above.
- Related: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V (fair round-robin), WL-0MTJE0FXC006WAOX (per-root cursor), WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7 (empty-file vs empty-backlog probe), WL-0MTF0KLO10043YAN (machine-wide leader).

## Desired change

Remove the time-based expiry of coordination entries. Replace it with a dispatch-time eligibility check (`fetchItem` + `classifyItemForDispatch` / audit-fresh check already in `dispatchFromCoordination`'s per-entry fetch) as the sole validity gate — stale entries are dropped at dispatch time, not by age.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — remove/neutralize `pruneStaleEntries` for machine file
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — remove prune call in `dispatchFromCoordination`; ensure per-entry `fetchItem`+classify is the eligibility gate (already present, but prune made it redundant)
- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` — leadership lease unchanged (only coordination expiry removed)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` — unchanged (consumes entries, not TTL)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` / `packages/herdr/README.md` — contract docs

## Related work

- WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V, WL-0MTJE0FXC006WAOX — round-robin
- WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7 — cooldown starvation probe
- WL-0MTF0KLO10043YAN — machine-wide leader
- WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 — dispatcher consumes Herdr list head (ranking, not expiry)

- **WL-0MSIG3G2X007RAEL** – events.ts: HerdrEventSubscriber socket module (completed)

## Summary
Make the leader's coordination check-in run every ~4 minutes (instead of 30) and renew its leader lock/lease at that cadence, so offers stay fresh and leadership is visibly healthy.

## Background
Parent WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P removes TTL prune — offers no longer expire by age — but operator asked: does the 30-min check-in mean scheduling only every 30 min? Answer: scheduling runs on idle ticks (every poll cycle when idle threshold met) against the coordination file; offers can be up to 30 min stale. Faster leader check-ins keep offers fresh and prove liveness.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Leader's coordination check-in interval is 4 minutes (configurable; default checkInIntervalMs overridden to 4*60*1000 for leader path) — leader recomputes and upserts its offer every ~4 min, not 30
- [ ] Non-leader instances keep the existing 30-min cadence (30*60*1000) — no extra wakeups
- [ ] During each leader check-in the leader renews its leadership lock/lease (refreshLease so another instance cannot steal leadership within the TTL) — ownership-based renewal, not validity-based
- [ ] Existing 5-min lease TTL (DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS=300) unchanged; 4-min renewal stays inside TTL with ~1 min grace
- [ ] Fail-safe preserved: missing/unreadable coordination or lease files degrade to no dispatch that cycle, never crash; check-in cadence does not spin-loop on errors
- [ ] Tests updated: leader check-in timing asserted at 4 min, non-leader at 30 min; lease renewal asserted on leader check-in

## Minimal Implementation
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts — introduce leader vs follower check-in intervals (e.g. LEADER_CHECK_IN_MS=4*60*1000, FOLLOWER_CHECK_IN_MS=30*60*1000); branch on isLeader / leaderState at tick; during leader check-in call leaderManager.refreshLease() (already per-tick self-heal, but ensure the check-in path explicitly renews)
- packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts — no TTL change
- Keep zero extra deps; respect per-worklog single-machine scope

## Dependencies
- Parent WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P (AC1 prune removed; offers persist — this item makes them fresher)

## Key Files
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts
- packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts
- docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md

**Constraint:** Do not reintroduce TTL prune on coordination entries (WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P AC1). Freshness comes from re-offer, not expiry.

## Goal

Root-cause the recurring `Downtime worker: 3 consecutive wl CLI errors — pausing dispatch for 3600000ms.` events that pause the downtime dispatcher for an hour across multiple projects, and fix the underlying cause so dispatch does not silently stall.

## Problem Statement

Every dispatch attempt in the observed window was followed ~90s later by a 60-minute pause (`three-strike rule`, `DOWNTIME_ERROR_STRIKE_LIMIT=3`). The pauses span every project:

- ContextHub: `14:56:21Z` pause (last dispatch `14:54:45Z`), no further dispatches in the 16:18–18:18Z window (0 in last 2h).
- open_source_llm: 10 dispatches 16:52–17:41Z, each followed ~90s later by a `3 consecutive wl CLI errors — pausing dispatch for 3600000ms.` entry (16:54, 16:58, 17:02, 17:06, 17:10, 17:14, 17:18, 17:22, 17:26, 17:43Z).
- AI_Hell: pause entries at `01:53, 15:23, 16:24, 17:55, 18:57Z` — no successful dispatch since `2026-09-02` (`downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`).
- SorraAgents / Tableau-Card-Engine: last dispatch `09-04 09:41` / `09-03 22:37`, then pause.

The machine-wide coordination file at snapshot held 2 stale ContextHub offers (`955073f2→WL-0MSLPM5ZB003TADT lastUpdated 16:16:45`, `ff2b1535→WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P lastUpdated 18:46:07`) that were never dispatched. The leader lease at the time was stale/expired (a fresh leader `045836e1` acquired only later at `19:03Z`).

The three-strike events log only the generic message — the underlying wl CLI error is NOT captured in `downtime-dispatches.log` (`recordError` writes `{cwd, at, message}` with the generic text). A work item WL-0MTL4PC0Y005GXTI ("Downtime pause log should include underlying wl error details") exists but the cause itself is still unknown: are these `SQLITE_BUSY` lock contentions, WAL growth/checkpoint stalls (WL-0MSG8EG7P002MX2I), sync-conflict loops (WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO — same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt; sync conflict resolution observed in sync.log during the window: `Conflict item=... type=same-timestamp ... chosen=local`), the `wl sync author-identity gate` pre-push block (OSL-0MT5Z8AJ7008LCQQ), or something else?

## User Stories

- As an operator, I want dispatches to stop being silently disabled for an hour, so downtime capacity is actually used.
- As a maintainer, I want the real wl error surfaced in the pause log (not just the generic message), so the cause is diagnosable without deep log archaeology.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Root cause identified** — RCA determines the concrete wl failure mode(s) behind the `3 consecutive wl CLI errors` strikes: reproduce or capture the actual stderr/error of the failing `wl` invocations (poll the logs, check `sync.log`/`downtime-dispatches.log`, run the failing commands manually, inspect `.worklog/logs/sync.log` conflict-resolution output in the window).
2. **Failure surfaces in the pause log** — the pause entry (or an accompanying entry) records the underlying wl error detail (per WL-0MTL4PC0Y005GXTI if not yet closed; otherwise this item supersedes it) so a future pause is diagnosable from the rolling log alone.
3. **Fix applied** — the root cause is fixed (code change in herdr/`wl`/sync/machine-coordination as appropriate): e.g. if `SQLITE_BUSY` → retry/backoff or WAL checkpoint fix; if sync-conflict loop → the same-timestamp merge fix (WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO) is completed; if author-identity gate → OSL-0MT5Z8AJ7008LCQQ fix lands; if leader-lease zombie → the lease-expiry fix (WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD) is confirmed deployed.
4. **Strikes no longer cascade** — after the fix, a normal idle run completes multiple dispatches without a `pausing dispatch for 3600000ms` entry after each one (verified over a 2h window or via unit/integration tests that simulate the failing CLI).
5. **No regressions** — full test suite green (`/skill:test`), including the downtime-worker, coordination-dispatch, and sync-conflict tests.
6. **Durable observability** — the dispatch/error log distinguishes strike causes so a recurrence is visible in one place (ties into the central-log work item).

## Constraints

- Do not disable or loosen the three-strike rule as the fix (it is a safety valve); fix the underlying failure.
- All work in a worktree per the implement workflow; do not edit main checkout.
- Push only to `dev`.

## Existing State / Evidence

- Pause entries (generic message) at the times listed above in each project's `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.
- `sync.log` shows sync-conflict resolution running DURING the window (same-timestamp conflicts chosen=local, lexicographic tie-break; `itemsUpdated=56`/`49` per sync).
- Related open items: WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO (sync-conflict loop), WL-0MSG8EG7P002MX2I (WAL growth/checkpointing), WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD (leader lease zombie), WL-0MTL4PC0Y005GXTI (pause log lacks wl error detail), OSL-0MT5Z8AJ7008LCQQ (author-identity gate blocks pre-push).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — three-strike rule, `recordError`, `wl` invocations.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps` (`getNextItem`, claim, `wl` child-process calls with `DOWNTIME_WL_TIMEOUT_MS=10s`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — `appendRollingJsonl` error entries.
- `.worklog/logs/sync.log` + per-project `.worklog/downtime-*.log` — evidence.

## Risks & Assumptions

- Assumption: the strikes share a common cause across projects (same machine, same herdr build, concurrent writers to shared SQLite/coordination files).
- Risk: transient contention that self-heals is hard to repro; mitigation is instrumentation (AC2) + capture real stderr before fixing.
- Risk: the cause may be multi-factor (sync conflicts AND lease expiry); RCA should rank contributors by evidence, not fix everything at once.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQI0XWYW005PDUF** – Remove Blessed TUI tests, CI artifacts & logs (completed)
- **WL-0MSG7ZTC000163FL** – Downtime worker test suite (test-first) (completed)

- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 03z, 10s, 45z, 57z, alone (+154 more)

# Intake Brief — Add a priority icon to the selection list (WL-0MTQYTA20009YXBT)

## Problem statement

The Herdr worklist selection list shows status, stage, producer review, and epic icons in its icon prefix, but the priority icon is only rendered as text after the title. Users scanning the list should see a priority icon alongside the other status indicators for at-a-glance prioritisation.

## Users

- **Primary**: Developers and operators using the Herdr worklist to browse and triage work items.
  - User story: "As a developer scanning the Herdr worklist, I want to see a priority icon as the first icon in each row so I can quickly identify urgent items without reading the full priority text."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The Herdr worklist selection list icon prefix (in `getIconPrefix` in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) includes a priority icon as the first icon, before the existing agent status slot.
2. The priority icon uses the existing `PRIORITY_ICONS` map from `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`: critical → 🚨, high → ⭐, medium → 📋, low → 🐢.
3. The priority icon respects the existing `noIcons` option — when icons are disabled, `PRIORITY_FALLBACK` text is shown instead.
4. The `ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH` is increased to accommodate the additional icon (from 12 to 13 cells), and alignment is preserved.
5. The work item `priority` field is already passed through the item type accepted by `getIconPrefix`.
6. All existing tests continue to pass; new tests are added for the priority icon in the prefix (emoji, fallback, null/undefined priority, noIcons mode).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.

## Constraints

- Must extend the existing `getIconPrefix` function in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — do not create a parallel icon system.
- Must preserve the existing `WL_NO_ICONS=1` / `noIcons` option behaviour.
- Must not break the fixed-width alignment (`ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH`) — adjust the constant if needed.
- Visual-only change in the Herdr worklist rendering; no persisted data model changes.
- The priority icon must appear **first** in the icon prefix row.

## Existing state

- **`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`**: The `getIconPrefix` function composes an icon prefix with columns: agent status (fixed-width slot), status icon, stage/audit icon, producer review flag, and optional epic icon. The `PRIORITY_ICONS` and `PRIORITY_FALLBACK` maps exist but are not used in the prefix.
- **`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`**: Calls `getIconPrefix(item, { noIcons })` and prepends the result before the item ID/title. The `item` type already includes `priority?: string`.
- **Priority text** is already rendered after the title as `${priorityIcon(item.priority, { noIcons })} ${item.priority}` (line 1255 of worklist.ts).

## Desired change

1. **`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`**:
   - Update `getIconPrefix` to prepend the priority icon as the first icon in the prefix.
   - The new column layout (left to right):
     - 0. Priority icon
     - 1. Agent status (existing fixed-width slot)
     - 2. Status icon
     - 3. Stage icon (for in_review items, shows audit-aware icon instead)
     - 4. Producer review flag
     - 5. Optional epic icon
   - Update `ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH` from 12 to 13 to account for the additional icon.
   - Update the JSDoc comment for `getIconPrefix` to document the new column layout.

2. **Tests**: Add/update tests for the priority icon in `getIconPrefix` (emoji, fallback, null/undefined priority, noIcons mode).

3. **Documentation**: Update any relevant documentation (e.g., `docs/icons-design.md` if it exists).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — Update `getIconPrefix` to prepend priority icon; update `ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — No changes needed (item type already includes `priority`)
- `tests/unit/icons.test.ts` — New tests for priority icon in `getIconPrefix`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-icons.test.ts` — Updated tests verifying priority icon in rendered prefix

## Related work

- **WL-0MQEI5DYO009736I** — "Add stage and audit result icons to TUI work item selection list" (completed) — established the pattern for adding icons to `getIconPrefix`.
- **WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9** — "Herdr selection list: metadata section should use the same icons as the list section" (completed) — ensured consistency between list and metadata sections.
- **packages/shared/src/icons.ts** — Core icon module; `PRIORITY_ICONS` map already defined.
- **packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts** — Worklist renderer that calls `getIconPrefix`.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk**: Adding a priority icon increases the icon prefix width from 12 to 13 cells, which may reduce available width for the item ID/title on narrow terminals. Mitigation: The existing truncation logic in `worklist.ts` already handles width overflow — it truncates lines to fit the terminal.
- **Assumption**: The `item.priority` field is always available on items displayed in the worklist. If `item.priority` is undefined/null, the priority icon function returns an empty string (handled by the existing `PRIORITY_ICONS` lookup with a default empty string).
- **Assumption**: The priority icon emoji (🚨⭐📋🐢) are all single-cell wide in the terminal, matching other icons in the prefix.
- **Scope creep mitigation**: Any additional features (e.g., priority-based colouring of the entire row, priority sorting changes, priority filters in the metadata panel) should be recorded as separate linked work items rather than expanding this item's scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Where should the priority icon appear in the icon prefix? The current order is: agent status, status icon, stage/audit icon, producer review flag, epic icon." — Answer: "The first icon in the row of icons in the selection list should be a priority icon." (from work item description). Final: priority icon is first in the prefix.
