## Summary

Make audit freshness **content-based** rather than write-time-based, by porting the
canonical content-fingerprint gate from the audit skill (SorraAgents,
SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT) into ContextHub.

Today `isAuditFresh()` (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) implements **only** the legacy
60 s time floor against `updatedAt`, so any metadata-only write (comment, sync merge,
lifecycle transition) marks a valid audit stale. A read-only review of the
`completed`/`in_review` queue found **22 of 52 items stale** and **12 with no audit at
all** (~65 % not fresh), almost none because the code actually changed.

## Problem

`updatedAt` is a *write* clock, not a *content* clock. It moves for reasons unrelated
to the audit's validity:

- `createComment` / `updateComment` / `deleteComment` unconditionally call
  `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()` (`packages/shared/src/database.ts`).
- sync merges re-timestamp items (95 items retimestamped to `2026-09-21T18:36:06` in a
  single sync; 244 items conflicted).
- `assignSortIndexValues()` (used by `wl migrate`) still bumps `updatedAt`.
- the audit runner's own verdict-driven status/stage transition happens *after* audit
  persistence and so stales the audit it just wrote.

The canonical algorithm is content-first, with the time gate only as a **legacy
fallback**:

> 1. fingerprint = HEAD sha + description hash + Key Files + working-tree state
>    (`git status --porcelain` + `git diff --name-only HEAD`); unchanged → fresh
> 2. time gate (floor): legacy reports use the 60 s gate

## Expected behaviour

- Each audit record carries a content fingerprint captured at persist time.
- `isAuditFresh` returns fresh when the stored fingerprint equals the current
  fingerprint, **regardless** of `updatedAt` movement caused by comments, sync merges
  or re-sorts.
- Audits without a fingerprint (legacy) fall back to the existing 60 s time gate.
- A genuine change to the auditable content (description/ACs, Key Files, HEAD,
  working-tree state) still invalidates the audit (stale).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `audit_results` gains a nullable `fingerprint` column via migration; existing rows
   are unaffected and remain readable.
2. `wl audit-set` (and the audit runner's `persist_audit.py` / `wl update --audit-text`
   path) records the fingerprint atomically with `audited_at`.
3. A single shared `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt, storedFingerprint, currentFingerprint)`
   helper is the sole freshness definition; it returns fresh when the fingerprints match.
4. `updatedAt` churn alone (post-audit comment, sync merge re-timestamp, `sortIndex`
   re-sort) does **not** mark a fingerprinted audit stale.
5. A change to the description/ACs, Key Files, HEAD sha, or working-tree state marks
   the audit stale.
6. Legacy audits with no stored fingerprint fall back to the existing time gate
   (unchanged behaviour).
7. `stageDisplayIcon`, `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate`, and the
   ordering predicate all consume the same shared helper — no competing comparison.
8. Tests cover: comment-after-audit stays fresh; sync-bump stays fresh; description
   edit goes stale; HEAD change goes stale; legacy fallback.
9. Full test suite passes.

## References

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE
- canonical algorithm: audit skill `SKILL.md` §Freshness Gate; SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT
- related-to: WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (P2 — sync-merge churn)
- evidence: `.worklog/logs/sync.log` (2026-09-21T18:35:58 → 18:36:17),
  `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` `isAuditFresh`, `packages/shared/src/database.ts`
  `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt`
data.title: Audit freshness: content-fingerprint gate as primary (port canonical fingerprint)

## Summary

Stop `updatedAt` acting as a catch-all write clock for **comments**, so that a
post-audit comment (session log, dispatch note, audit note, close reason) can no
longer invalidate a valid audit.

## Problem

`createComment`, `updateComment` and `deleteComment` in
`packages/shared/src/database.ts` all call `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()`
unconditionally. The icon freshness predicate (`isAuditFresh`,
`AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS = 60000`) only tolerates comment bumps that
land inside 60 s of the audit. In practice comments arrive minutes or days later:

- `WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT`: audit `22:04:23`, `updatedAt 22:05:44` — 81 s, just past the
  window.
- `WL-0MTOBZZNU0009MW1` (+ 4 siblings): the `implement` "Start phase aborted" comment
  is the last write before the cluster that staled the audit.

The audit skill already documents this hazard and prescribes ordering (comment
**before** `wl audit-set`), but ordering is fragile and cannot protect against any
comment added later by another session or bot.

## Expected behaviour

- Comment activity is still recorded and visible (ordering, recency, FTS), but it does
  not move the audit-relevant timestamp.
- Semantic content edits (title, description, ACs, tags, parent, status, stage,
  priority, issue type, risk, effort) continue to bump the content timestamp.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A separate activity timestamp (e.g. `activityAt`) is introduced and bumped by
   comment create/update/delete; `updatedAt` is left untouched by comment writes.
2. Audit freshness is computed against the content timestamp, not the activity
   timestamp.
3. Ordering/recency features that currently rely on comment-updated `updatedAt`
   continue to work (or are explicitly re-pointed at `activityAt` with tests).
4. `WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT`-class case (audit then transition/comment > 60 s later) stays
   fresh.
5. Tests: add comment after audit → still fresh; delete comment → still fresh;
   description edit after audit → stale.
6. Full test suite passes.

## References

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE
- related-to: WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9 (audit freshness after post-audit comments),
  WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R (flag-only flips must not invalidate audits)
- audit skill `SKILL.md` §Safety/prompt design — ordering contract SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM

## Summary

Ensure a just-persisted audit is not invalidated by the audit runner's **own**
verdict-driven lifecycle transition.

## Problem

`persist_audit.py` / `wl audit-set` writes the audit and (atomically) sets
`updatedAt = auditedAt`. The runner then applies the terminal status/stage
transition separately (`_apply_terminal_lifecycle`). Because `status` and `stage`
are tracked content fields, that second `wl update` bumps `updatedAt` **after** the
audit, so the item is stale the moment the audit completes.

Observed: `WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT` audit `2026-09-20T22:04:23.765Z`, `updatedAt`
`2026-09-20T22:05:44.810Z` — 81 s, just outside the 60 s tolerance. The audit skill
explicitly notes the tolerance "covers the runner's own writes only"; 81 s is
ordinary, so the window is simply too small to be relied on.

## Expected behaviour

- After a successful audit run, the item is fresh immediately and remains fresh until
  real content changes — the runner's own transition never stales its own audit.
- The lifecycle transition still happens and is still recorded.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The audit is the **last** write for a just-audited item: `auditedAt >= updatedAt`
   after the runner completes (persist `auditedAt` after the lifecycle transition, or
   tag the runner's own transition so freshness ignores it).
2. `isAuditFresh` returns true for the `WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT` shape (audit then
   transition ~80 s later) without widening the global tolerance constant.
3. A genuine post-audit content edit (description/ACs) still stales the audit.
4. Regression test covering the runner's persist→transition ordering.
5. Full test suite passes.

## References

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE
- audit skill `SKILL.md` §Safety/prompt design — ordering contract SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM
- `persist_audit.py`, `_apply_terminal_lifecycle`

## Summary

Remove the second, competing audit-freshness definition and route every consumer
through the single shared helper.

## Problem

There are two freshness definitions with different semantics:

1. `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`:
   `auditTime > updateTime - AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS` (60 000 ms,
   one-sided).
2. `packages/shared/src/database.ts` `isAuditNotReadyFresh()`:
   `new Date(audit.auditedAt).getTime() >= new Date(itemUpdatedAt).getTime()`
   (strict `>=`, no tolerance) — used by the ordering boost
   (`sortItemsByScore`, `computeScore`, `selectBySortIndex`).

So the icon and downtime dispatcher can call an item fresh while the ordering tier
treats it as stale (or vice versa) — the exact divergence WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE set out
to remove, which only unified the icon and dispatch paths.

## Expected behaviour

- Exactly one freshness definition exists in the codebase.
- The ordering path, the icon path and the dispatch path agree for every input.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `isAuditNotReadyFresh` is removed or delegates to the shared `isAuditFresh`.
2. No other file re-implements an `auditedAt` vs `updatedAt` comparison.
3. Symmetric at-or-near semantics are used where intended (`|auditedAt - updatedAt| <
   tolerance`), matching the canonical SorraAgents fix, rather than the current
   one-sided comparison.
4. Tests assert icon, dispatch and ordering agree on: fresh, stale, just-persisted,
   and missing-audit inputs.
5. Full test suite passes.

## References

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE
- related-to: WL-0MSI3XH34001LLU4 (SorraAgents at-or-near canonical fix)

## Summary

Make child-audit coverage explicit so a child covered by a parent audit is not
treated as "no audit" by the icon and the downtime dispatcher.

## Problem

11 of the 12 `completed`/`in_review` items with **no** audit record are children
(e.g. `WL-0MTQ48YKS000PA6H`, `WL-0MU2LF6SZ000JQYI`, `WL-0MU2LFC1Y0077U1U`,
`WL-0MU2LFHBH004VF48`, `WL-0MUAG2S77003JGDL`, `WL-0MTF5WNRB009RHRU`). A parent audit
covers them (child verdicts are reused), but there is no record on the child itself.

Consequences:

- `stageDisplayIcon` falls back to the plain stage icon (no ✅/⏳), so the queue looks
  unaudited.
- `selectAuditCandidate` filters `!isAuditFresh(c.auditedAt, c.updatedAt)`; a child
  with no `auditedAt` is therefore always a candidate, so the downtime worker
  re-dispatches a redundant child audit — which writes and creates more churn.

## Expected behaviour

- A child covered by a parent audit is recorded as covered (inherited/parent audit
  reference or equivalent), and is not re-dispatched or shown as unaudited.
- A child genuinely not covered by any audit is still surfaced for audit.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Policy decided and documented: either (a) every child gets its own verdict, or
   (b) a child may record an inherited audit reference to its covering parent audit.
2. If (b): the `audit_results`/work-item model can express an inherited coverage
   reference; `isAuditFresh` (or its caller) treats a covered child as fresh.
3. `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate` do not dispatch a child already
   covered by a fresh parent audit.
4. `stageDisplayIcon` shows the audit result (or an explicit "covered by parent"
   indicator) for covered children.
5. Tests cover: covered child not dispatched; uncovered child still dispatched;
   parent audit becomes stale → child becomes a candidate again.
6. Full test suite passes.

## References

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE
- audit skill `SKILL.md` §in-main-slot mode (child-verdict reuse)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `selectAuditCandidate`

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I need the 13:54:33Z re-dispatch of LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO traced to a specific
selection path and mechanism, so the fix targets the real code path instead of a hypothesis.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4** (RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches CRITICAL implement
items). Covers parent **AC1**.

# Context

Planning established that the hypothesis set in the parent description is not sufficient on its own:
the Herdr-head critical-first scan (`selectCriticalFirstCandidates`) only accepts
`status === 'open' || 'blocked'` items, and `dispatchClaimedTier` performs a CAS claim on the
expected `status`+`stage`. A duplicate therefore requires the item to be **genuinely `open` at the
expected stage** at re-dispatch time — i.e. H1 (marker bypass) alone cannot duplicate; H2/H5 (the
item's `status` reverts to `open` while a dispatch pane is still live) is the necessary partner. That
is exactly the scenario the escalation path was built for, and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
already documents it ("a previous dispatch was rolled back / the implementing agent aborted and reset
the item to `open` while the standing marker remained").

The incident root log is **not present on this host**: `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py`
over the five default roots finds no `LP-*` entries at all. AC1 must therefore be satisfied by
targeted instrumentation and reproduction, which AC1 explicitly sanctions.

Also note the second dispatch vector: the coordination leader "validates offers at dispatch-time
without a marker check" (same doc), so the coordination path must be traced too.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC1.1 — RED witness.** A characterisation test drives **two idle cycles** in one process against a
critical `plan_complete` (implement-kind) item that is observed `open` at its marker's stage while its
dispatch pane is live, and asserts exactly `1` dispatch. The test **fails** against the pre-fix code
and records the observed dispatch count.

**AC1.2 — Confirmed selection path.** The RCA verdict names the confirmed selection path (Herdr-head
critical-first scan vs coordination offer dispatch) with a source line reference and a cycle-by-cycle
trace (cycle 1: selected/accepted, cycle 2: selected/accepted + claim outcome + marker state).

**AC1.3 — Hypothesis decision table.** Each of H1 (critical-first bypasses marker exclusion), H2
(stale item status in the dispatcher snapshot), H3 (non-atomic rolling-log rewrite), H4 (multiple
leaders) and H5 (item `status` reverted to `open` while a pane is live) is marked **confirmed** /
**refuted** / **not reproducible**, each with the discriminating evidence. H2/H5 is explicitly
confirmed or refuted.

**AC1.4 — Residual uncertainty.** Any hypothesis left open is recorded with the workaround F3/F4
apply for it, and the residual risk is stated.

**AC1.5 — CAS/bypass analysis recorded.** The verdict states whether the duplicate required a real
DB `status: open` (CAS succeeds) or a CAS gap, so F3's guard is justified rather than assumed.

# Minimal implementation

- Add a deterministic two-cycle harness around `dispatchDowntimeWork` using the existing injectable
  seams: `getHerdrListHead`, `getNextItem`, `claimItem`, `spawnAgentPane`, `recordDispatch`,
  `getRunningDowntimePanes`.
- Simulate the live pane via the `herdr pane list` fixture path (`parseHerdrPaneListOutput` /
  `countRunningDowntimePanes`) so the same data shape the dispatcher sees in production is used.
- Simulate the status revert by returning the item as `open` in cycle 2's Herdr head while the marker
  written in cycle 1 stands.
- Capture the per-cycle selection reason (a precursor to the AC6 schema) so the verdict is auditable.
- **Parent AC1 (restated):** The selection path and mechanism that produced the 13:54:33Z re-dispatch of LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO are confirmed (H1: critical-first scan bypasses marker exclusion / H2: stale item status in dispatcher snapshot / H3: non-atomic rolling-log rewrite / H4: multiple leaders) via targeted instrumentation or reproduction.

# Dependencies

None. This is the first item in the sequence.

# Deliverables

- RCA verdict comment on parent WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4 (decision table + trace + line references).
- New test block in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (the RED witness; promoted to the
  permanent suite by WL-WL-0MUBVKS5I007LSWB).

# Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`
- `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

# Out of Scope

- Implementing the fix (WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO/WL-WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI).
- Multi-leader support (parent out-of-scope).

item already in-flight produce exactly one dispatch on **both** dispatch paths, so the duplicate cannot
silently return.

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC5.1 — Herdr-head path.** Two consecutive idle cycles over a Herdr head containing a critical
`plan_complete` implement item **already claimed/in-flight at the same stage** produce **exactly one**
dispatch (asserted on dispatch count, not only on the returned outcome).

**AC5.2 — Coordination path.** The same two-cycle assertion passes for the coordination path
(`computeMostImportantItem` → offer → leader dispatch).

**AC5.3 — Stale-marker coverage.** At least one case covers a non-critical candidate at the same stage
with a **stale** marker, so the suite guards against a critical-only regression.

**AC5.4 — Live-pane variants.** The suite covers: live `working` pane (must block), `done` pane (must
not block), `exited` pane (must not block), and a failed/unparseable pane query (must not duplicate).

land and GREEN after; the RED/GREEN transition is recorded as the dependency evidence on those items.

data.description:
# Goal

As a herdr operator, I want the critical-first escalation to skip an item that already has a live
dispatch pane, so a critical item whose `status` reverted to `open` is never dispatched twice, while
escalation of genuinely stuck critical items is preserved.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4**. Covers parent **AC2** and **AC3**.

# Design (approved at the plan approval gate)

The critical-first scan currently bypasses the dispatched-marker exclusion **unconditionally**
(WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT). This replaces the unconditional bypass with a **stale-only bypass gated on an
item-scoped live-pane check**, with a marker-TTL fallback when the pane query is unavailable:

```
for a critical-first candidate:
  1. resolve the item-scoped in-flight signal (live dispatch pane whose label suffix is the item id
     and whose agent status is non-terminal)
  2. if a live WORKING pane exists                 -> SKIP  (reason: in-flight-pane)
  3. else if the pane query SUCCEEDED and found none -> ESCALATE (reason: no-live-pane)
  4. else (pane query FAILED/unparseable)          -> fall back to the marker TTL:
       fresh marker (age <= markerStaleWindowMs)   -> SKIP  (reason: in-flight-unverified)
       stale/absent marker                         -> ESCALATE (reason: marker-stale-escalation)
```

This deliberate **neither-blind-fail-closed-nor-blind-fail-open** choice was confirmed at the approval
gate: escalation is never starved permanently (the TTL fallback keeps progressing), and a duplicate is
never permitted while a pane is live. Note the fallback is benign in practice — pane spawn itself needs
herdr, so a persistent pane-query failure also prevents dispatch.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC2.1 — Live pane blocks.** With a live `working` downtime pane whose label suffix is the item id,
**no** dispatch is attempted for that item — regardless of marker freshness, stage advancement, or
`status` being `open`.

**AC2.2 — Fail-closed on unknown in-flight state.** A failed or unparseable pane query never results in
a dispatch that could duplicate in-flight work; it resolves via the marker-TTL fallback (AC3.3) and
records the `in-flight-unverified` reason.

**AC2.3 — Terminal panes do not block.** Panes whose agent is absent, `done`, or `exited` do not block
dispatch (no idle-pane deadlock).

**AC2.4 — Item-scoped only.** The guard never uses a global running-pane count as a dispatch limit —
the WL-0MU2EP6JL006A1U3 invariant is preserved (that count stays a liveness/owner-lease signal only).

**AC2.5 — Normal loop covered.** The guard also applies to critical candidates reaching dispatch
through the normal (non-critical-first) loop, so AC2 holds "regardless of selection path".

**AC3.1 — Escalation preserved.** A critical item with a fresh **or** stale marker and **no** live pane
is still escalated within one idle cycle; all existing critical-first tests stay green.

**AC3.2 — Escalation is bounded.** Deferral happens only while a live working pane exists or while the
marker is fresh during a pane-query outage — never by an unbounded fixed TTL alone.

**AC3.3 — TTL fallback documented.** The fallback bound (`markerStaleWindowMs`, default 24h, floor 1h)
and its rationale are documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

# Minimal implementation

- Add an item-scoped in-flight resolver, resolved **once per idle cycle** and threaded into
  `dispatchFromHerdrList`: extend `RunningPanesResult` to expose pane records (or add a sibling dep
  returning `{paneId, itemId, kind, agentStatus}[]`), reusing `parseHerdrPaneListOutput`.
- Derive the item id from the pane label suffix (`buildDowntimePaneTitle` preserves `- <itemId>` as a
  suffix via `truncatePaneTitlePreservingSuffix`).
- Replace the critical-first loop's unconditional marker bypass with the decision table above.
- Factor the resolver so WL-WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI can reuse it unchanged (no logic duplication across paths).
- Fail-open on resolver errors in the sense that the resolver returns "unavailable" (never throws into
  the dispatch loop); fail-closed semantics are the decision table's step 4.
- **Parent AC2 (restated):** A critical-priority item is never dispatched twice for the same skill while a prior dispatch is in-flight (live pane and/or unexpired claim), regardless of marker freshness or stage advancement.
- **Parent AC3 (restated):** The critical-first escalation path retains its ability to progress items blocked by a stale marker, without re-dispatching in-flight items. Escalation is bounded (e.g., once per claim TTL, or gated on a live-pane / in-flight check).

# Dependencies

- WL-WL-0MUBVKS5I007LSWB (regression suite — must exist to prove AC5.5's RED→GREEN transition).

# Deliverables

- Code + unit tests + `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` update (§"Critical-first tier & freeze
  split-by-skill").
- RED→GREEN evidence comment referencing the WL-WL-0MUBVKS5I007LSWB suite.

# Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I want the coordination leader to withhold or reject an offer whose item already
has a live dispatch pane, so the coordination path cannot produce the duplicate that the Herdr-head fix
(WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO) prevents.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4**. Covers parent **AC2**.

# Context

`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` states the coordination leader "validates offers at dispatch-time
**without a marker check**". That is a second, independent duplicate-dispatch vector: the Herdr-head fix
alone would leave it open, which is why AC5 names both paths and why this is a separate work item
(decision Q7 at the plan approval gate: keep F3 and F4 separate).

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC2.6 — Offer withheld when in-flight.** An offer for a critical item with a live `working` dispatch
pane is not offered (or is rejected at leader dispatch) and the rejection reason is recorded in the
coordination log.

**AC2.7 — Fallback candidate chosen.** `computeMostImportantItem` does not offer an in-flight critical
item; when another offerable item exists it is chosen instead, and the dispatcher does not fall through
to an empty cycle.

**AC2.8 — Cross-root correctness.** The pane query uses the **offer's own root** (`opts.cwd`), never the
leader pane's root — the WL-0MTQ14W7L003II5A cross-root invariant is preserved and asserted.

**AC2.9 — No duplication of logic.** The in-flight resolver is the one factored in WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO; this item
does not reimplement label parsing or pane-status filtering.

**AC2.10 — Leader-side re-check.** Even when an offer was computed before the pane appeared, the
leader's dispatch-time validation rejects it (time-of-check/time-of-use gap closed).

# Minimal implementation

- Resolve the in-flight set for the offer's root inside the offer computation and again at
  leader dispatch time.
- Reuse the WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO resolver; if F3 factored it into a shared helper, import it unchanged.
- Record the withheld/rejected outcome with the reason so it is visible in the coordination log and in
  the AC6 schema.
- **Parent AC2 (restated):** A critical-priority item is never dispatched twice for the same skill while a prior dispatch is in-flight (live pane and/or unexpired claim), regardless of marker freshness or stage advancement.

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I want the dispatch and coordination rolling logs written atomically, so a
concurrent marker read can never observe an empty or partial log and momentarily lose a
duplicate-dispatch marker.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4**. Covers parent **AC4**.

# Context

`appendRollingJsonl` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`) rewrites the log non-atomically: read all
lines → push → trim → `writeFile` directly to the target path. A reader arriving during the
`writeFile` can see a truncated or empty file, which makes `dispatchedItemMarkers` /
`dispatchedItemStages` momentarily lose the marker. This is a contributing factor (H3 in the parent
RCA), not the sole cause — it cannot by itself duplicate a critical-tier item, because the
critical-first scan bypasses markers entirely (that is WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO's fix). It is fixed independently
because it is a genuine TOCTOU defect and because it silently weakens every marker-guarded tier.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC4.1 — Atomic replacement.** `appendRollingJsonl` writes to a temporary sibling file and `rename`s it
over the target. A test asserts the target path is never opened for direct writing.

**AC4.2 — No leaked temp files.** No temporary file remains after a successful append, and none remains
after an I/O failure (cleanup happens before the error is rethrown).

**AC4.3 — Concurrent reader never sees a partial log.** A test that hammers append + read in parallel
observes **only** complete, parseable JSONL lines — never an empty file, never a partial line. The test
fails against the pre-fix writer.

**AC4.4 — Contract unchanged.** Trimming to `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES` (100) and the throw-on-I/O-failure
(fail-closed) contract are unchanged; the file stays human-readable JSONL.

**AC4.5 — Both logs.** Both `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` and the coordination log use the atomic
writer.

**AC4.6 — Same-filesystem rename.** The temp file is created in the same directory as the target so
`rename` is atomic (a cross-device rename would fall back to copy + unlink and lose atomicity).

# Minimal implementation

- Temp file name including pid + random suffix, in the same directory as the target.

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I want every dispatcher log entry to record the session/pane id and the selection
path/reason, so the next duplicate-dispatch RCA is answerable from the log alone instead of by
inference.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4**. Covers parent **AC6**.

# Context

The current schema is `itemId/kind/dispatchedAt/cwd/title/stage`. Two constraints shape the design:

1. `recordDispatch` runs **before** `spawnAgentPane` (fail-closed ordering: a marker write failure
   aborts the dispatch), and `DowntimeSpawnResult` is `{ok: true}` with no pane id — `send-to-pi.sh` is
   fire-and-forget. The pane/session id is therefore **not** known at marker-write time.
2. `dispatchedItemMarkers` takes the **last** entry per `itemId`, and `markerStillExcludes` is
   fail-closed on a missing/unparseable `dispatchedAt`. Any post-spawn entry must therefore **preserve**
   `dispatchedAt` + `stage` or it would corrupt marker semantics.

Decision at the plan approval gate (Q5): use a **best-effort post-spawn enrichment entry** rather than
extending the spawn contract / `send-to-pi.sh`.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC6.1 — Selection path and reason recorded.** Every successful dispatch entry records
`selectionPath` (e.g. `critical-first` | `normal-scan` | `coordination-offer` | `scheduled-prompt`) and
a machine-readable `selectionReason` (e.g. `marker-stale`, `in-flight-pane`, `no-live-pane`,
`in-flight-unverified`, `non-critical`).

**AC6.2 — Pane/session id recorded without breaking markers.** Successful dispatches record the
resolved pane id via a post-spawn enrichment entry that **preserves** `itemId`, `kind`, `stage` and
`dispatchedAt`; a test round-trips the enriched log through `dispatchedItemMarkers` and
`markerStillExcludes` and proves identical exclusion/release behaviour with and without enrichment.

**AC6.3 — Enrichment is fail-open.** If the pane id cannot be resolved, the dispatch still succeeds and
the log records an explicit absence (no guessed value).

**AC6.4 — Backward compatible.** Legacy entries without the new fields parse and behave exactly as
before; the existing `downtime-log.test.ts` compatibility tests stay green.

**AC6.5 — Tooling reports the new fields.** `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py` surfaces
`selectionPath`/`selectionReason`/`paneId` for post-fix evidence (and tolerates their absence).

**AC6.6 — Spawn-failed entries unchanged.** `outcome: 'spawn-failed'` entries stay non-excluding
(WL-0MT32F908002YFFA AC2 invariant) with or without the new fields.

# Minimal implementation

- Add `selectionPath`, `selectionReason` and an optional `paneId` to `DowntimeDispatchEvent`.
- Thread the selection path/reason from the selection loops (WL-WL-0MUBVKPLP006RRDJ's per-cycle trace provides the
  vocabulary; WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO/WL-WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI provide the in-flight reasons).
- After a successful spawn, resolve the pane id (label-suffix lookup against `herdr pane list`) and
  append the enrichment entry, swallowing errors exactly like the existing spawn-failed trace.
- Extend the scan script's output fields and the documented log schema.
- **Parent AC6 (restated):** Each dispatcher log entry records the session/pane id and the selection path/reason, extending the current schema (`itemId/kind/dispatchedAt/cwd/title/stage`) to support automated RCA.

# Dependencies

- WL-WL-0MUBVKPLP006RRDJ (defines the selection-path/reason vocabulary from the confirmed mechanism).

# Deliverables

- Code + tests + `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` log-schema update + scan-script field support.

# Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

As a herdr operator, I want reproducible evidence that no new duplicate dispatch occurs after the fix,
so I can trust the fix beyond the test suite and know exactly how to re-verify it.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4**. Provides the observational evidence for parent **AC2**.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC-V1 — Full suite green.** `npm test` passes with WL-WL-0MUBVKPLP006RRDJ's RED witness and WL-WL-0MUBVKS5I007LSWB's regression
suite GREEN (no skipped or quarantined tests).

**AC-V2 — No new duplicates in the observation window.**
`python3 packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py --since <fix-deploy ISO-8601>` over the five
default roots reports **zero** new duplicate pairs for the dispatch kinds touched by WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO–WL-WL-0MUBVL251006JAQ0

**AC-V4 — Bounded window stated.** The window length is stated together with its limitation (a short
window cannot prove absence of a rare race); the claim is limited to "no observed recurrence in the
window".

**AC-V5 — Test-failure triage.** Any failure found is triaged into a critical `test-failure` work item
via the test skill (`check_or_create.py`) before this item is advanced to `in_review`.

discovered-from: WL-0MU8807BI008C9ME

## Problem

The report skill (`~/.pi/agent/skills/report/scripts/render_report.py`) renders `Audit: ❔ not run` for items whose audit IS persisted and passing.

Root cause: `_fetch_work_item` reads `data.get('workItem', {})` and then `work_item.get('auditResult')` (line ~235). Since the Worklog migration, `wl show <id> --json` exposes the structured audit at the TOP LEVEL (`result.auditResult` — an object with `readyToClose`, `auditedAt`), while `workItem.auditResult` is the legacy field and is always null. The renderer expects a boolean, so it always falls through to 'not run'.

Observed on WL-0MU8807BI008C9ME: `wl show --json` top-level auditResult={readyToClose:true}, but the rendered report said 'Audit: not run'.

## Fix

Read the top-level `auditResult` object and map `readyToClose` -> passed/failed; fall back to the legacy boolean if present.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A passing persisted audit renders `Audit: passed`.
2. A `readyToClose:false` audit renders `Audit: failed`.
3. An item with no audit renders `Audit: not run`.

# Ship-mode guard: block entry while project work is in progress, freeze on confirm

**Headline:** The herdr worklist gains a pre-dialog guard that refuses to open the Ship It confirmation dialog while any live agent pane (any workspace) is working on a work item belonging to the project, listing the blocking panes/work items; on `ship` confirmation it writes the Code Freeze marker immediately and clears it if the release command fails to dispatch.

## Problem statement

The herdr worklist lets an operator enter Ship It (dev→main release) mode even while other agent panes are actively working on the same project, risking a release of half-finished work. The worklist must refuse to open the Ship It confirmation dialog while any live agent pane in any workspace is working on a work item belonging to the project being shipped, tell the operator which panes/work items are blocking, and — once the operator confirms with `ship` — place the project into Code Freeze immediately (before the release command is dispatched).

## Users

- **Producers / release managers** using the herdr worklist who trigger dev→main releases.
- **Other agents** working on the project, who rely on the Code Freeze marker to refuse new implementation while a release is running.
- **User story:** "As a producer, when I press `S` to ship, I want the worklist to refuse and tell me which panes are still working so I do not ship over in-flight work. Once I have closed them and type `ship`, I want the freeze to apply at once so no agent starts new work mid-release."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Pressing the Ship It shortcut (`S`) when one or more **live** agent panes (machine-wide, across all herdr workspaces) carry a work-item ID belonging to the current project's worklog does **not** open the Ship It confirmation dialog. A notice is shown instead listing the offending work-item IDs (and pane labels where available) and stating that ship mode cannot be entered until the work is completed and those panes are closed.
- [ ] The blocking check runs **before** the confirmation dialog is rendered; the dialog is never shown while blocking panes exist.
- [ ] A pane only blocks when it hosts a **live** agent: a pane whose agent is absent, `done`, or `exited` does not block, even when its label carries a project work-item ID.
- [ ] When no blocking pane exists, pressing `S` opens the Ship It confirmation dialog exactly as today (no regression), and typing `ship` + Enter dispatches `/skill:ship release` as before.
- [ ] On typing `ship` + Enter (the confirm action), the worklist writes the Code Freeze marker at `<worklog-dir>/code-freeze.json` with `{ "active": true, "reason": "...", "startedAt": "<ISO>", "pid": <pid> }` **before** dispatching `/skill:ship release`.
- [ ] If dispatching `/skill:ship release` fails (no agent pane available, `onCommand` throws, or the dispatch is a no-op), the worklist **best-effort removes the Code Freeze marker it just wrote** and surfaces the error, so no stale freeze blocks the project once the release never started.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: the guard with blocking and non-blocking pane sets (live vs `done`/`exited` agents), multiple blocking panes, work-item IDs from a different project not blocking, the blocked-notice content, the pre-dialog gating (dialog not opened when blocked), the marker write on confirm, and the marker cleanup on dispatch failure.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and the Code Freeze marker contract docs.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Fail-open for browsing, fail-safe for the guard.** The existing Code Freeze reads are deliberately fail-open (a broken marker never blocks browsing). The new guard must fail *closed* only in the sense of not shipping on ambiguous pane data: an unreadable `herdr pane list` or `wl list` must not silently allow the ship dialog — surface the uncertainty rather than pretending the project is clear. (Decide and document the exact behaviour in implementation; recommendation: treat an unavailable pane/item query as "cannot verify — do not ship" and show the notice.)
- **No new dependency.** Reuse the existing primitives: `parseHerdrPaneListOutput` / `HerdrPaneRecord` (`downtime-worker.ts`), `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` (`hydrator.ts`), and the `code-freeze.ts` marker contract.
- **Project membership by work-item ID, not prefix.** Match pane-label IDs against the actual set of work-item IDs in the current project's worklog. A shared ID prefix across projects must not cause a false block.
- **Code Freeze marker ownership changes.** The marker is currently written/cleared by the ship skill and only read by the herdr plugin. This work extends the contract so the plugin writes the marker on Ship It confirmation; the ship skill remains the authority that clears it on release exit. Update the contract documentation accordingly.
- **No regression to the Ship It dialog.** The typed-confirmation behaviour (case-insensitive `ship`, Enter to confirm, Esc to cancel, bottom-anchored overlay) is unchanged.
- **ANSI rendering.** Any notice reuses the existing in-pane notice/dialog rendering helpers (`formatCodeFreezeDialog` pattern); no new dependencies.
- Follow build → test → commit discipline (vitest suite in `packages/herdr`).

## Existing state

- **Ship It shortcut / dialog** — `packages/herdr/src/ship-it-dialog.ts` (`ShipItDialogState`, `formatShipItDialog`, `overlayShipItDialog`) and `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (`SHIP_IT_COMMAND = '/skill:ship release'`, `openShipItDialog()`, dialog key handling in `onData`). The dialog is opened from the chord-resolution branch when the resolved command equals `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`.
- **Code Freeze marker** — `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.ts` provides read-only helpers (`readCodeFreezeState`, `isCodeFreezeActive`, `readCodeFreezeStatus`, `readCodeFreezeStatusForRoot`) for `.worklog/code-freeze.json`; there is currently **no writer** in the plugin. The ship skill writes/clears the marker around the release.
- **Project ↔ pane matching** — `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` already lists in-progress items (`wl list --status in-progress`) and active panes (`herdr pane list`, machine-wide) and matches work-item IDs embedded in pane labels via `extractWorkItemIdsFromText`. `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` guarantees spawned pane titles preserve the work-item ID suffix, so labels reliably carry the ID.
- **Blocked-work UI precedent** — the Code Freeze notice (`code-freezeNotice` flag, `formatCodeFreezeDialog`, dismissal key handling in `worklist.ts`) is a full-pane modal used when an implement action is blocked.
- **Toast feedback** — `packages/herdr/src/notify.ts` (`showToast`) is fire-and-forget and may not be reliably seen; a blocking guard should use the in-pane modal notice pattern instead.

## Desired change

1. **New guard module** (e.g. `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.ts`): pure, injectable helpers to
   - collect the current project's work-item IDs from `wl list --json`;
   - list machine-wide panes from `herdr pane list` (reusing `parseHerdrPaneListOutput`);
   - return the **blocking** panes: panes whose label carries a project work-item ID and whose agent is live (agent present, status not `done`/`exited`);
   - format the blocked-notice text listing the offending work-item IDs / pane labels.
   Unit-test the pure logic with fixture panes (no real `wl`/`herdr`).
2. **Pre-dialog gate in `worklist.ts`**: when the resolved command is `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`, run the guard *before* `openShipItDialog()`. If blocking panes exist, set a modal notice (listing the panes) and return without opening the dialog. The notice dismisses like the Code Freeze notice (Esc/Enter/q) and never dispatches.
3. **Immediate Code Freeze on confirm**: in `openShipItDialog`'s `onConfirm`, write `.worklog/code-freeze.json` (extend `code-freeze.ts` with a writer, e.g. `writeCodeFreezeMarker()` / `clearCodeFreezeMarker()`) before calling `executeResolvedCommand(SHIP_IT_COMMAND, ...)`. On dispatch failure / no-op, best-effort clear the marker it wrote and show the error.
4. **Tests**: a focused `ship-guard.test.ts` for the pure guard, plus TUI integration tests (in the style of `code-freeze-dialog.test.ts` / `ship-it-dialog-tui.test.ts`) that drive `S` with a real marker dir + injected pane resolver, covering blocked and clear paths and the confirm-time marker write/cleanup.
5. **Docs**: update `packages/herdr/README.md` (Ship It + Code Freeze sections) and the Code Freeze marker contract docs to record the new pre-dialog guard and the plugin-writes-on-confirm ownership change.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.ts` — **new** guard module: project-item-ID set, blocking-pane filter, notice formatter (pure/injectable).
- `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.test.ts` — **new** unit tests for the guard.
- `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.ts` — add marker **writer/clearer** (currently read-only); document the plugin-writes-on-confirm contract extension.
- `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.test.ts` — tests for the new writer/clearer.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — pre-dialog gate in the `SHIP_IT_COMMAND` branch; modal blocked notice; marker write + cleanup in `openShipItDialog`'s confirm handler.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — reuse `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` (no change expected; reference).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — reuse `parseHerdrPaneListOutput` / `HerdrPaneRecord` (no change expected; reference).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the guard and the marker-ownership change.
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` / code-freeze contract docs — record the plugin-writes-on-confirm contract.

## Related work

- `Code Freeze: herdr plugin blocks implement actions (banner + dialog) during ship-it process (WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR)` — completed; the code-freeze banner/dialog and marker contract this guard extends.
- `Add Ship It shortcut with typed confirmation dialog in TUI selection screen (WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY)` — completed; the Ship It dialog whose `openShipItDialog()` is the gate point.
- `Code freeze should be in place from ship skill start, not just run-release.js execution (WL-0MT8MYGL3009QUZ6)` — completed; establishes that the freeze must start early, motivating the on-confirm write.
- `Downtime dispatcher must honour ship-it code freezes (no new implementations during freeze) (WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY)` — completed; the fail-closed consumer of the marker.
- `Implement: code-freeze detection, banner, implement-command blocking and dialog (herdr plugin) (WL-0MSBUCG73003MV3S)` — completed; the freeze infrastructure and dismissal patterns to reuse.
- `Herdr hydrator: rescue in_progress work items with no active pane (WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI)` — completed; the project ↔ pane matching primitives reused by the guard.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (producer, Q1 = a):** "work that is ongoing" means any live agent pane whose label carries a work-item ID from the current project — i.e. the rule is pane-presence, not item status. A completed item whose pane is still open still blocks; the operator must close it. Confirmed by the producer.
- **Assumption (producer, Q2 = list):** the blocked notice lists the offending work-item IDs (and pane labels where available) so the operator has an action list. Confirmed by the producer.
- **Assumption (producer, Q3 = cleanup):** on dispatch failure the plugin best-effort clears the freeze marker it wrote and surfaces the error. Confirmed by the producer.
- **Risk: ambiguous pane/item data.** If `herdr pane list` or `wl list` fails, the guard cannot verify. Recommendation: do not open the dialog and show the notice (fail-safe against shipping over unknown work); document the choice.
- **Risk: plugin-written marker left stale** if the plugin process dies between writing and dispatch, or the ship skill never clears it. Mitigation: clear on dispatch failure (Q3); document manual removal (`rm .worklog/code-freeze.json`) for the crash case.
- **Risk: performance.** Queries run on `S` keypress only; cache within the keypress to avoid a double `wl list`/`herdr pane list`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** blocking other actions (close/audit) during the pre-check, or scanning other projects' worklogs, is out of scope — record as separate work items if desired.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What constitutes 'work ongoing' in a project?" — Answer (producer): **(a)** any live-agent pane whose label carries a work item ID belonging to the current project — pane-presence, not item status. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "How should panes across workspaces be discovered?" — Answer (research): reuse `herdr pane list` (machine-wide, all workspaces) + `wl list` with the ID-matching already implemented in `hydrator.ts`. No cross-project `agent-panes.json` scan needed. Source: code inspection (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`).
- Q: "What message should be shown when ship mode is blocked?" — Answer (producer): **list** the offending panes/work-item IDs. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Should the blocked state be overridable?" — Assumption: not overridable; the operator closes the panes and retries. Source: requirement text ("cannot enter ship mode until work has been completed and panes have been closed"); no override requested.
- Q: "Who writes the code-freeze marker on confirm?" — Answer (requirement + producer): the herdr plugin writes the marker at confirm time, extending the current contract in which only the ship skill writes it. Source: requirement text; producer Q3 answer.
- Q: "Should the marker be cleared if the ship command fails to dispatch?" — Answer (producer): **cleanup** — best-effort clear and surface the error. Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

> Machine-generated by the `find-related` skill (keywords extracted from the seed description). The manual list under [Related work](#related-work) above is the curated set; the matches below may include low-relevance false positives and are retained only for auditability.

# Ship Guard Module — `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.ts`

## Summary
Pure, injectable helper module to guard ship-mode entry by detecting live agent panes working on project work items.

## Parent AC Coverage
This task covers parent ACs 0, 1, 2:
- Parent AC 0: "Pressing the Ship It shortcut (`S`) when one or more **live** agent panes ... does **not** open the Ship It confirmation dialog." — `formatBlockedNotice` and `listBlockingPanes` produce the blocking notice; the guard module enables the pre-dialog gate.
- Parent AC 1: "The blocking check runs **before** the confirmation dialog is rendered." — the guard module returns the blocking set before any dialog logic runs.
- Parent AC 2: "A pane only blocks when it hosts a **live** agent: a pane whose agent is absent, `done`, or `exited` does not block." — `listBlockingPanes` filters by agent status (not `done`/`exited`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `collectProjectWorkItemIds()` runs `wl list --json` and returns a `Set<string>` of all work-item IDs in the current project's worklog.
- [ ] `listBlockingPanes(projectIds, paneListOutput)` calls `herdr pane list`, extracts work-item IDs from pane labels, filters to panes whose labels carry a project work-item ID and whose agent is live (not `done`/`exited`), and returns the blocking panes.
- [ ] `formatBlockedNotice(blockingPanes)` formats human-readable text listing offending work-item IDs and pane labels.
- [ ] All logic is pure and injectable — no direct file I/O or side effects in the helpers; callers pass command output strings.
- [ ] On query failure (wl list or herdr pane list unavailable), the guard fails safe: listBlockingPanes returns the full set as blocking and the caller must not open the dialog.

## Minimal Implementation
- New file: `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.ts`
- Exports: `collectProjectWorkItemIds`, `listBlockingPanes`, `formatBlockedNotice`
- Dependencies: `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` (hydrator.ts), `parseHerdrPaneListOutput`/`HerdrPaneRecord` (downtime-worker.ts)
- Pure functions that accept command-output strings as arguments (testable without real processes).

## Deliverables
- `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.test.ts`

# Pre-dialog gate in worklist.ts + Code Freeze on confirm

## Summary
Integrate the ship guard into the worklist's Ship It flow: pre-dialog gate that blocks opening the confirmation dialog when live panes exist, and write the code-freeze marker on confirm before dispatching the release command, with best-effort cleanup on failure.

# Herdr mode-switch: raise default operator-idle threshold from 15 to 30 minutes

## Problem statement

The herdr plugin's activity-gated proxy mode-switch worker (WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9) drops
the llama-proxy to **cheap** mode once the operator has been idle. The default idle
window is currently 15 minutes
(`DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 900_000`), which proves too aggressive:
the operator stepped away only briefly and the proxy had already restarted onto the
cheap (local-first, 2-slot) pool, costing a mode-switch restart plus a later restart
back to fast.

The default should be **30 minutes**.

User story:

- *"As the operator, when I look away from the worklog for a few minutes, I do not
  want the proxy to drop to cheap mode; the default idle window should be 30 minutes
  so only a genuine absence triggers the switch."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` in `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` is `1_800_000` (30 minutes) and its doc comment states 30 minutes.
- [ ] The `clampModeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` doc comment references the 30-minute default (invalid/negative input falls back to the new default).
- [ ] The `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` field doc in `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` states the new default (`1_800_000` / 30 min).
- [ ] The value is still overridable per-install via the existing `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` setting; the 60-second floor is **unchanged**.
- [ ] Unit tests assert the new default (`packages/herdr/src/settings.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-integration.test.ts`), and the clamp test still passes with the new default; `900_000`-based explicit-threshold fixtures in `mode-switch-worker.test.ts` remain valid (they pass the threshold explicitly).
- [ ] Documentation updated to state the new default: `packages/herdr/README.md` (settings section, `900000` = 15 minutes → `1800000` = 30 minutes) and `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md` settings table.
- [ ] No behavior change other than the default value: per-slot operator gate, fast-switch-on-command, fail-closed semantics, single-flight/dedup, poll interval and its clamps are all untouched.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes.

> **Note:** `CHANGELOG.md` is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline and is excluded from this list.

## Constraints

- **Surgical change.** Only the default constant, the comments that state it, the tests that assert it, and the two docs that record it change. Do not refactor the worker.
- **The 60s floor stays.** `MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_FLOOR_MS` is unchanged; only the fallback/default moves.
- **No new setting.** This is a default change, not a new option; consumers still read the same `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` key.
- Build → test → commit discipline (vitest suite in `packages/herdr`).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts:79` — `export const DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 900_000;` with a `/ ** Default idle window before switching to cheap mode: 15 minutes. * /` comment (line 78) and `clampModeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` doc at line ~114 mentioning the "15-minute default".
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts:90,125,233-235` — field doc, `defaultSettings`, and load-time clamp fallback all route through the exported constant.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1429`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:6166` — consumers reading `s.modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs ?? DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` (no change needed; they pick up the new default).
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` — extensive explicit `idleThresholdMs: 900_000` fixtures; only the clamp assertion exercises the default symbolically.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.test.ts:167-186` — `'defaults to 900_000 ms (15 minutes)'` describes the default explicitly.
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-integration.test.ts:119` — `expect(DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS).toBe(900_000); // 15 minutes`.
- `packages/herdr/README.md:688-689`, `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md:57` — document the default.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` — default constant + comments
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — field doc comment
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.test.ts` — default assertion + title
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-integration.test.ts` — default assertion
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — settings documentation
- `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md` — settings table

## Related work

- **WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9** – Herdr plugin: activity-gated proxy mode switching (cheap on operator idle, fast on operator command) — completed; the feature whose default this item retunes.
- **WL-0MT9F67Y3008S0PR** / **WL-0MT9FL9JO002JEAZ** – per-slot operator gate for the cheap switch — completed; the gate semantics that remain unchanged.
- **WL-0MT1EDYS0002CMUK** / **WL-0MT1EECPU0024Z7J** – mode-switch settings validation, clamps and integration — completed; the clamp contract preserved here.
- **WL-0MU6MXCZZ007ZXT9** – mode-switch flip-flop / leader election — open, unrelated to the threshold value.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the "default" the operator wants raised is the shipped default for fresh installs (and the fallback for invalid settings), not a forced override of an existing user's saved `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs`. Existing installs that already persisted 900000 keep their value; only the default changes. Recorded because a forced migration was not requested.
- **Risk: low.** A constant change with test/doc updates; no control-flow change. The 60s floor and all fail-closed paths are untouched.

# `a-y` audit approve silently no-ops: `audit_results` missing `fingerprint` column on existing databases

## Summary

Pressing the `a-y` (audit approve) chord on an `in_review` item appears to do nothing. The chord runs:

```
wl reviewed <id> false && wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close yes --summary 'Approved by manual review'
```

`wl reviewed` succeeds, but `wl audit-set` fails with:

```
Error: Failed to persist audit result for <id>
  table audit_results has no column named fingerprint
```

Because the chord is configured `open_pane: false`, the command runs detached in the background with stdout/stderr redirected to a per-run log file under `/tmp/herdr-background-logs/`. The non-zero exit is never surfaced in the TUI, so the operator sees no error and the audit is never recorded. The same failure affects `a-r` (audit reject) and any other `wl audit-set` caller on an affected database.

## Users

- **Producers / human reviewers** who approve or reject `in_review` items with the `a-y` / `a-r` chords.
- **Agents** whose `persist_audit.py` / `wl audit-set` audit persistence silently fails on affected databases.

### User story

As a producer reviewing an `in_review` work item, when I press `a-y` I expect the audit to be recorded as approved and the item to be ready to close. Instead nothing changes and no error is shown.

## Root cause analysis

1. **Schema change without an automatic upgrade path.** Commit `dd62b3f6` (WL-0MUBVH5S0008NQ9K) added a nullable `fingerprint TEXT` column to the `audit_results` table and updated `saveAuditResult` / `getAuditResult` to read/write it (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`). It also added migration `20260923-add-audit-fingerprint` (`src/migrations/index.ts`).
2. **`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` does not alter existing tables.** Databases created before that commit have an `audit_results` table without `fingerprint`. The migration that would add it exists but is only applied by `wl doctor upgrade --confirm`; migrations are not applied automatically on CLI startup, and `SCHEMA_VERSION` was not bumped.
3. **`saveAuditResult` now unconditionally references the column.** The prepared `INSERT ... fingerprint ...` statement fails on any database whose `audit_results` table lacks the column, so every audit write fails.
4. **The failure is silent for the `a-y`/`a-r` chords.** Both entries set `open_pane: false` (`packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`), so `spawnBackgroundShell` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`) runs the command detached and writes output only to a log file. Nothing surfaces the non-zero exit in the TUI.

## Evidence

- Direct reproduction:

  ```
  $ wl audit-set AH-0MUAYB5UK0052P1D --ready-to-close yes --summary 'Approved by manual review'
  Error: Failed to persist audit result for AH-0MUAYB5UK0052P1D
    table audit_results has no column named fingerprint   # exit 1
  $ wl audit-show AH-0MUAYB5UK0052P1D --json
  { "success": true, "workItemId": "AH-0MUAYB5UK0052P1D", "audit": null }
  ```

- Schema check (read-only) on both affected databases:
  - AI_Hell `.worklog/worklog.db`: `audit_results` has no `fingerprint` column; `metadata.schemaVersion = 8`.
  - ContextHub `.worklog/worklog.db`: same — `audit_results` has no `fingerprint` column; `schemaVersion = 8`; no `audit_fingerprint_added` marker.
- `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run` lists `20260923-add-audit-fingerprint` (safe=true) as pending.
- Repeated background logs confirm the user's repeated `a-y` presses all failed identically:

  ```
  /tmp/herdr-background-logs/herdr-2026-09-23T14-59-50-691Z-1048204-wl-reviewed-AH-0MUAYB5UK0052P1D-false-wl.log
  needsProducerReview set to false for AH-0MUAYB5UK0052P1D
  Error: Failed to persist audit result for AH-0MUAYB5UK0052P1D
    table audit_results has no column named fingerprint
  ```

  (5 log files between 14:57 and 14:59 on 2026-09-23.)

## Impact

- **Broad:** every database created before `dd62b3f6` cannot persist audits through `wl audit-set`, the `a-y`/`a-r` chords, or the audit skill's `persist_audit.py` path.
- **ContextHub itself is affected** — its own `.worklog/worklog.db` lacks the column, so audits of ContextHub items cannot be recorded.
- **Silent:** the failure is invisible for background shortcuts, so operators may believe an item was approved when it was not.

## Desired behaviour

- Auditing (`wl audit-set`, and therefore `a-y`/`a-r` and the audit skill's persister) works on any supported database, including those created before the `fingerprint` column was introduced, without requiring the operator to know about and run a manual migration.
- A database whose schema is missing a column that the current code requires is upgraded (or the required column is ensured) as part of normal CLI operation, or the command fails with a clear, actionable error naming the exact remediation — never a raw SQLite error swallowed into a log file.
- Background (`open_pane: false`) shortcut failures are surfaced to the operator (e.g. a herdr toast/notice) rather than only written to a log file.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit persistence works on legacy databases.** Given a database whose `audit_results` table was created before the `fingerprint` column existed (e.g. the schema produced by migration `20260604-add-audit-results`), running `wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close yes` succeeds and `wl audit-show <id>` returns the persisted audit. No manual `wl doctor upgrade` invocation is required, or the CLI itself performs the safe upgrade as part of the command.
2. **Schema version is consistent.** The `fingerprint` column is covered by the schema versioning/upgrade mechanism so that a database at the current `SCHEMA_VERSION` is guaranteed to have it, and legacy databases converge on upgrade. If `SCHEMA_VERSION` must be bumped to make this true, it is bumped.
3. **Clear failure if upgrade cannot proceed.** If the required column cannot be added (e.g. read-only database, permission error), the command fails with a clear message that identifies the missing column and the remediation (`wl doctor upgrade --confirm`), not a bare SQLite error.
4. **Background shortcut failures are surfaced.** A non-zero exit from an `open_pane: false` shortcut (e.g. `a-y`, `a-r`) is surfaced to the operator in the herdr TUI (toast/notice), including the command and a short error excerpt, instead of only being written to the log file.
5. **Regression tests.** Tests cover: (a) `wl audit-set` against a legacy `audit_results` schema (without `fingerprint`) persists successfully; (b) a fresh database still persists audits; (c) the migration/upgrade path is idempotent and sets the `audit_fingerprint_added` marker; (d) herdr surfaces a background-shortcut non-zero exit (unit test of the failure-surfacing helper).
6. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes (worklog vitest + herdr vitest).
7. **Documentation updated** where relevant — e.g. `CLI.md` / `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` notes on schema upgrades, and the herdr `README.md` note on background shortcut error surfacing.

## Immediate remediation (for affected databases)

Running `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` in the affected project applies the pending safe migrations (including `20260923-add-audit-fingerprint`) and restores `wl audit-set`. This unblocks the operator now but is not a substitute for AC1–AC4 (operators should not have to know this).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `audit_results` schema, `saveAuditResult` / `getAuditResult` / `saveAuditResults`; candidate site for ensuring the column exists.
- `src/migrations/index.ts` — `20260923-add-audit-fingerprint` migration and `runMigrations` / `listPendingMigrations`.
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` — `wl audit-set`; where a clear remediation error should surface.
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — `wl doctor upgrade` entry point.
- `src/cli-utils.ts` / `src/database.ts` — database open path; candidate site for an automatic safe upgrade.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `spawnBackgroundShell` / `spawnBackgroundPi`; background failure surfacing.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `a-y` / `a-r` entries (`open_pane: false`).
- `packages/herdr/src/notify.ts` — `showToast` for surfacing failures.
- `tests/audit_results_table.test.ts`, `tests/migrations.test.ts`, `tests/cli/audit-results-cli.test.ts` — schema/migration/CLI tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — background dispatch tests.

## Related work

- **WL-0MUBVH5S0008NQ9K** — *Audit freshness: content-fingerprint gate as primary (port canonical fingerprint)*: introduced the `fingerprint` column, the `saveAuditResult` change, and migration `20260923-add-audit-fingerprint`. This item is the direct cause of the regression on existing databases.
- **WL-0MS95CEAE0080EB4** — *a-y (audit approve) shortcut does nothing — should run wl command visibly in a herdr pane*: earlier, unrelated root cause (dead `CMD:` path); this item is the follow-on failure now that the command does run.
- **WL-0MSVVFBJ2003RRYK** — *Audit lifecycle: verify status/stage transition after persist (silent failure leaves items in idea)*: precedent for treating silent persistence failures as high severity.
- **AH-0MUAYB5UK0052P1D** — *Symbols for weapons do not reflect what the weapon does* (AI_Hell): the item the reporter was trying to approve when the bug was found (`discovered-from:AH-0MUAYB5UK0052P1D`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** automatic application of *safe* migrations on database open is acceptable; if not, the fallback is a clear, actionable error and an explicit upgrade prompt. The implementer should confirm the intended policy.
- **Risk:** auto-migrating on open could mask genuine version mismatches; limit to idempotent `safe: true` migrations and keep backups/`wl doctor upgrade` for the rest.
- **Risk:** surfacing background failures could spam toasts; debounce/aggregate per command run.
- **Out of scope:** the separate `initializeSchema` vs migration-sentinel drift (why `20260315-add-audit`, `20260604-*` also show as pending) unless it blocks AC1/AC2.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `test/tmp_mig/worklog.db` is no longer tracked and `test/tmp_mig/` is gitignored.
2. Running the full suite leaves `git status` clean (no binary churn).
3. `test/migrations.test.ts` still passes.

# Ship guard always shows "Cannot verify pane state — cannot enter ship mode."

discovered-from:WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW — defect in the ship-mode guard feature (`packages/herdr`).
**Component:** `packages/herdr` — `createProductionShipGuardQuery` / `runShipGuard`.
**Severity:** High — the new ship gate is effectively always-on (permanently blocks ship mode) and shows a misleading reason.

## Symptom

Pressing `S` to open the Ship It dialog shows:

```
⚠ Cannot verify pane state — cannot enter ship mode.
Unable to check whether other panes are working on project items.
Please retry when the herdr CLI or worklog is available.
```

…even though `herdr pane list` works and open panes are actively working on the project. The notice lists no blocking panes (there is no action list for the operator).

## Root cause

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (`createProductionShipGuardQuery`) runs `wl list --json` with `maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024` (8 MiB):

- `worklist.ts:3939` — `buildWlArgsForRoot(cwd, ['list', '--json'])` / `buildWlArgs(['list', '--json'])`
- `worklist.ts:3940-3943` — `exec('wl', wlArgs, { timeout: DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS, maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024 })`

The project's `wl list --json` output is **8,549,046 bytes** (2,298 work items) — **160,438 bytes over** the 8,388,608-byte limit. Node's `execFile` therefore rejects with:

```
ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER: stdout maxBuffer length exceeded
```

The `catch` around the `wl` call sets `worklogOutput = null` (`worklist.ts:3944-3946`). That makes `queryFailed === true` (`worklist.ts:5036`), so `runShipGuard` returns `ok: false` (`ship-guard.ts:216-222`) and the caller renders the generic `queryFailed` notice (`ship-guard.ts:167-172`).

The `herdr pane list` query succeeds (≈12,516 bytes) — only the **worklog** query overflows.

### Reproduction

```bash
cd /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub
wl list --json | wc -c        # 8549046
node -e "const {execFile}=require('child_process');const {promisify}=require('util');
promisify(execFile)('wl',['list','--json'],{encoding:'utf8',maxBuffer:8*1024*1024})
 .then(()=>console.log('ok')).catch(e=>console.log('THREW',e.code))"
# -> THREW ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER
```

## Why the message is misleading

- The notice says it "cannot check whether other panes are working on project items", but the pane query is fine; the failing query is the **project work-item ID set**.
- Because the worklog parse never happens, `blockingPanes` is empty, so the operator gets **no list of the offending panes/work-items** — defeating the "list the offending panes so the operator can close them" acceptance criterion (WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW) in this failure mode.
- It will not self-heal: the worklog only grows, so `wl list --json` will keep exceeding 8 MiB.

## Notes / contributing design

The guard needs the **full** set of project item IDs (a pane carrying a completed item still blocks — producer-confirmed semantics), so it loads the entire worklog. Building an ID set from an unbounded ~8.5 MB (growing) payload with a fixed 8 MiB `maxBuffer` is fragile. Possible directions (to be decided in implementation): raise the `maxBuffer`; add a `wl` IDs-only/bounded query; stream `wl list`; or match panes by a targeted per-ID lookup instead of loading all IDs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `createProductionShipGuardQuery` no longer fails when `wl list --json` output exceeds 8 MiB (clear-path guard still evaluates panes).
- [ ] A regression test covers a `wl list --json` payload larger than the previous `maxBuffer` (e.g. injected large output), proving the guard parses it and evaluates blocking panes.
- [ ] When the worklog query genuinely fails, the blocked notice distinguishes "worklog unavailable" from "pane list unavailable" so the operator knows which query failed.
- [ ] Full `packages/herdr` vitest suite passes.
- [ ] Documentation/comments reflecting the fix are updated.
data.title: Ship guard always reports 'Cannot verify pane state': wl list --json (8.5 MB) exceeds the 8 MB maxBuffer

## Problem Statement

The `detect_regressions()` function in `generate_standup.py` has a Python operator-precedence bug. The condition on line 754:

```python
if is_regressed and in_window(item, ...) and cur_status in (...) or cur_stage in (...) or cur_status != "completed" or cur_stage != "in_review":
```

In Python, `and` binds tighter than `or`, so the expression parses as:

```python
(is_regressed and in_window(...) and cur_status in (...))
or (cur_stage in (...))
or (cur_status != "completed")
or (cur_stage != "in_review")
```

The `in_window()` check is effectively bypassed by the trailing `or` clauses. Any item that was completed+in_review in the pre-window snapshot but is currently not in that state gets flagged — regardless of when it changed.

## Impact

- 51 false-positive regressions reported (items that regressed days/weeks ago)
- Only 1 true regression was present in the window
- Standup report becomes noisy and untrustworthy

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Fix the operator-precedence bug so `in_window()` gates all branches correctly. The fix is a simple parenthesisation: `if is_regressed and in_window(item, window_start, window_end):`
2. Add a regression test that reproduces the bug (pre-window completion changes must not be flagged) and verifies the fix (in-window completion changes must be flagged).
3. Build and all tests pass.
data.title: Standup skill: regression detection flags all previously-completed items (operator-precedence bug)

# Downtime dispatcher stalls when llama-proxy serves slots:[] + slots_stale:true

Parent RCA: WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28. Discovered while verifying the parent's AC1 against the LIVE proxy during implementation of the four children.

## Evidence (live proxy, 2026-09-24)

`GET http://192.168.0.199:8000/llama/local/status`:

```json
{"active_query":true,"local_active_query":true,"model_switch_in_progress":false,"current_model":"Qwen3","llama_server_running":true,"available_slots":1,"total_slots":3,"slots_stale":true,"slots":[],"local_owner_session_id":["http://localhost:8080","herdr-1790261458-1799601-10619"],"local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds":645.5}
```

## Root cause

`parseLlamaStatus` accepts `slots: []` as a valid empty array and ignores the `slots_stale` field entirely. In `tick()`:

- `perSlotMode = Array.isArray(status.slots) && 0 < requiredFreeSlots < total_slots` -> **true** for `slots: []` (an empty array is still an array).
- `perSlotTracker.record([])` starts no timers -> `thresholdMetCount === 0 < requiredFreeSlots` -> `ready === false` -> tick returns `!ready` (idle, no dispatch).
- Even if `ready` were true, `slotOwned = countFreeUnownedSlots([]) === 0` -> true -> refusal.
- `freeSlots = countFreeUnownedSlots([]) = 0`.

When `slots` is absent (not `[]`), the count-based fallback is also blocked: the derived `local_lease_active` is true (owner array + 645 s lease), so `globalIdleChecks` fails.

Result: with `slots: []` / `slots_stale: true` and an active lease, the dispatcher NEVER dispatches — the RCA stall persists despite the child-1 per-slot fix (WL-0MU8807BI008C9ME).

## Proposed fix areas (to be planned)

1. Treat `slots_stale: true` (and/or an empty `slots` array) as "no per-slot identity": parse the flag and fall back to the count-based path.
2. In the count-based path, do not let a lease block dispatch when `available_slots >= requiredFreeSlots` and `total_slots > 1` (spare capacity) — only a truly owned SOLE slot should block.
3. Add a regression test pinned to the exact live payload above.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A payload with `slots: []`, `slots_stale: true`, `total_slots: 3`, `available_slots: 1`, an owner lease and a live dispatched pane dispatches into the free slot(s) (per-slot mode is not entered on stale/empty data).
2. A count-based multi-slot payload with spare `available_slots` and a held lease no longer blocks dispatch.
3. A count-based single-slot payload with a held lease still refuses (preserve WL-0MU8809SZ0022VZG AC3).
4. A contract test pins `slots_stale` parsing and the empty-array fallback.

## Notes

- Blocks the parent RCA's AC1 ("dispatches resume during agent runs").
- Child WL-0MU8807BI008C9ME's comment already anticipated this follow-up ("If cheap-mode responses also serve slots=[] ... perSlotMode is false and the stall persists").
data.title: Downtime dispatcher stalls when llama-proxy serves slots:[] + slots_stale:true (per-slot mode has no identity; count-based fallback lease-blocked)

# Herdr extension crashes at init: TDZ ReferenceError on modeSwitchWorker

## Symptom

Opening the worklist tab (prefix+l) opens the tab but the plugin crashes on initialization:

```
Worklog plugin error: ReferenceError: Cannot access 'modeSwitchWorker' before initialization
    at Object.config (packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1611:15)
    at createDowntimeWorker (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:4821:63)
    at main (packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1583:42)
```

Reproduced directly: `cd packages/herdr && npx tsx src/index.ts </dev/null` exits 1 with the error above.

## Root cause (temporal dead zone)

- `createDowntimeWorker` calls `opts.config()` SYNCHRONOUSLY during construction (`downtime-worker.ts:4821`, `disableMarkerExists(opts.config().cwd)`).
- The `config` closure passed from `index.ts` evaluates `modeSwitchWorker.getLastKnownMode()` (index.ts:1611).
- `modeSwitchWorker` is declared with `const` **after** `downtimeWorker` (index.ts:1624), so the reference hits the TDZ and throws.

Introduced by the combination of:
- `6188a90d` (WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME) — added the `mode: modeSwitchWorker.getLastKnownMode()` field to the config closure.
- `88a14451` (WL-0MU6MXCZZ007ZXT9) — moved `modeSwitchWorker` creation to AFTER `downtimeWorker`.

There is already a `modeSwitchHolder` declared BEFORE `downtimeWorker` (index.ts:1562) for exactly this kind of forward reference (used by `onProxyIdle`).

## Fix

Use the existing holder in the config closure:

```ts
// index.ts config closure
mode: modeSwitchHolder.worker?.getLastKnownMode() ?? undefined,
```

At construction `modeSwitchHolder.worker` is undefined -> `undefined` (conservative PARALLELISM=1); after `modeSwitchHolder.worker = modeSwitchWorker` is assigned, later ticks read the real mode. No TDZ.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `npx tsx src/index.ts` no longer throws "Cannot access 'modeSwitchWorker' before initialization" / "Worklog plugin error" at startup.
2. Mode-aware Phase 2 parallelism is preserved: once the mode-switch worker exists, `config().mode` returns its last-known mode.
3. A regression test guards the plugin startup path (no TDZ / no init crash).
4. Build + full test suite green; commit pushed to dev.
data.title: Herdr extension crashes at init: TDZ ReferenceError on modeSwitchWorker in downtime config()

Implementation decisions (child of WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN):

1. **Schema**: Added `PaneCloseLogEntry` (entryType 'pane-close', timestamp, itemId, itemTitle, paneId, kind, outcome, reason, reasonCode, closed) + `appendPaneCloseLogEntry` (fail-closed). `DowntimeLogEntry` extended with optional entryType/paneId/enrichment/reasonCode.

data.author: pi
data.comment:
Implementation design notes (pre-finish):

1) AC1 leader-gating: the cheap idle switch is gated on the existing downtime leader (DowntimeWorker.isLeader) via a live isLeader() probe — no separate election. Non-leaders skip tick() entirely (no proxy fetch, no mode read, no POST). The fast switch fired from onOperatorCommand remains on all instances: the operator's active pane may not be the downtime leader, so gating fast on leadership would leave the proxy in cheap while the operator is actively working (contradicting AC4 'the proxy remains in fast mode while the active pane receives commands'). Only the cheap switch — the flip-flop source — is leader-gated, matching AC1's '(cheap POST)' wording. This is a deliberate, documented deviation from the brief's desired-change note #4 ('only leader fires fast POST').

2) AC2/AC6 shared activity: every instance writes mode-activity.json (atomic temp+rename, monotonic max) into getMachineCoordinationDir() ?? join(targetCwd, '.worklog') — the same directory as the downtime leader lease. The leader's idle evaluation uses max(local clock, shared timestamp), so the proxy stays fast while any pane has recent activity. Shared read failure falls back to the local clock (fail-closed, AC6).

3) AC3 threshold: the default was raised 15->30 min by WL-0MUDVBKH00009OGY (completed, manual review) during this item's lifetime, and that item scoped this one as 'unrelated to the threshold value'. This item's AC3 explicitly requires 3_600_000 (60 min), so the shipped default is now 60 min; existing installs keep their persisted override (no forced migration). Assumption recorded: AC3 is honoured as written (60 min) despite the intervening 30-min default. The 60s floor is unchanged.

4) AC5 leadership transitions: the probe is read live each tick, and the leader reads the shared activity file on every tick, so a handover is honoured on the next tick with no spurious switch.

Verification so far: herdr typecheck green; full herdr suite 2502 tests / 68 files green; root build green.
